sharing: build the link-first flow from ADRs 0023 to 0028
OPEN
v2-build,comp:engine
post-cutover
This umbrella builds the link-first sharing flow. The invite link is the primary sharing path. There is no approve step: any owner device converts a claim by itself. A link holder reads the folder at once from the link blob. Revocation follows the link-first model: a link revoke cuts the link holders, and the owner can also remove the people who joined through the link. A scope root takes many grants. A grantee name is a label, not an identity. The invite page shows a preview before join.

## Decisions

- [ADR 0023](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0023-the-invite-link-is-the-primary-sharing-path-and-conversion-runs-by-itself.md): The invite link is the primary sharing path and conversion runs by itself
- [ADR 0024](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0024-a-link-holder-reads-at-once-from-the-link-blob.md): A link holder reads at once from the link blob
- [ADR 0025](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0025-revocation-under-the-link-first-model.md): Revocation under the link-first model
- [ADR 0026](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0026-a-scope-root-takes-many-grants.md): A scope root takes many grants
- [ADR 0027](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0027-a-grantee-name-is-not-an-identity.md): A grantee name is not an identity
- [ADR 0028](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0028-the-invite-page-previews-before-join.md): The invite page previews before join

The blueprint is already reworded for these ADRs: `CONTEXT.md`, `blueprint/core.md`, `blueprint/engine.md`, `blueprint/api.md`, `blueprint/web-client.md`, `blueprint/testing.md`.

## PR batches

Engine slices come first. The web slices come after them.

| Batch | Issues | Ownership |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A | #1964, #1965, #1966 | crates/core seal + KATs |
| B | #1967, #1968 | invite_mint, accept, link_read |

## Accepted residuals

- [ADR 0024](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0024-a-link-holder-reads-at-once-from-the-link-blob.md) E4: The link URL can unmask membership.
- [ADR 0025](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0025-revocation-under-the-link-first-model.md) E8: The link kind and the deadline are in the clear.
- [ADR 0024](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0024-a-link-holder-reads-at-once-from-the-link-blob.md) E5 / [ADR 0025](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0025-revocation-under-the-link-first-model.md) E5: Archived records stay readable after a cut.
- [ADR 0023](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0023-the-invite-link-is-the-primary-sharing-path-and-conversion-runs-by-itself.md) E5 / [ADR 0025](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0025-revocation-under-the-link-first-model.md) E4: A removed person can join again through another live link.
- [ADR 0023](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0023-the-invite-link-is-the-primary-sharing-path-and-conversion-runs-by-itself.md) E4: When the owner is offline past the deadline, the claim is lost.
- [ADR 0025](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0025-revocation-under-the-link-first-model.md) E3: A co-writer can hide a nested scope from the sweep.

- [ADR 0023](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0023-the-invite-link-is-the-primary-sharing-path-and-conversion-runs-by-itself.md) E6: Claimants can fill the mailbox of the owner.
- [ADR 0024](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0024-a-link-holder-reads-at-once-from-the-link-blob.md) E3: Each link has one key.
- [ADR 0025](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0025-revocation-under-the-link-first-model.md) E7: A person revoke ends the link for holders that are not converted yet.

# #1959 engine: two owner devices can publish different records at one sequence

## Problem

Two devices of the same owner can publish the same scope root at the same time. Both derive the same name key from the scope seed (`crates/engine/src/session.rs:205-211`), so the network cannot tell them apart. The drain builds on the cached scope root and does not resolve it fresh first (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:2113-2152`). The sequence is the local floor plus one (`crates/engine/src/net/publish.rs:334`), and the drain passes `min_current_sequence: None` (`drain.rs:5911`). So both devices sign sequence N+1 with different bytes.

After the PUT the engine reads the name back (`publish.rs:381-404`). The same sequence with different bytes is `Unconfirmed`; the loser halts the attempt and keeps the op at the head of the queue (`drain.rs:5922-5927`), then rebases and retries (`drain.rs:1760-1771`, `crates/engine/src/sync/rebase.rs:489-531`). That reconciles the op. It does not reconcile the network: one routing endpoint can keep device A's N+1 record and another device B's, and readers then depend on endpoint order (`crates/engine/src/net/fanout.rs:250-255` keeps the first endpoint at a tie).

`blueprint/engine.md:115-121` says "CAS publishes embed the exact expected sequence" and "a lost race re-resolves and rebases". The code checks no server-side expected sequence, and the drain does not re-resolve before it signs. `publish.rs:120-128` still says "rebase is a later slice".

## Expected

A publish from a stale base must not land at the same sequence as a sibling device's record. Either the drain re-resolves the root and signs strictly above the highest sequence it observed, or the publish carries the expected sequence and the routing layer refuses a mismatch, per the blueprint rule. The read-back must classify a same-sequence different-bytes record as a lost race, not as unconfirmed.

## Notes

Found during the sharing wayfinder map while deciding how two owner devices convert the same invite claim. Sharing now takes the mailbox ack as its lock, so this issue is independent of that map.

Local verification in my worktree: `cargo fmt --all --check` clean; `cargo clippy -p cipherbox-engine --all-targets -- -D warnings` clean; the four new tests pass. Against `main`'s source with the PR's tests kept, the `net.rs` test and two drain tests fail; `a_sibling_root_at_the_same_sequence_is_a_lost_race_the_next_pass_heals` passes either way (the PR body does not claim otherwise). Tree restored; no repository edit remains. Scratch artifacts: `~/.claude/scratch/w1963/C/review/{pr.diff,simplify.patch,test.log,clippy.log,without-fix*.log}`.

## Findings

### F1 — should-fix — CONFIRMED — `crates/engine/src/net/publish.rs:383-391`, `crates/engine/src/net/fanout.rs:250-256`

Defect: the confirm compares only the single freshest record the fan-out picks, and the fan-out keeps the FIRST endpoint on a sequence tie, so a same-sequence sibling on a later endpoint reads as `Published`.
Failure scenario: A and B both mint N+1. If A's bytes sit on endpoint 0 (or endpoint 0 is transiently `Err` for A at confirm time), A reads its own bytes back: `Published`. B reads its own bytes from its first endpoint: `Published`. Both self-adopt N+1 and dequeue. The split is never healed; the next resolve on either device takes the other's N+1 as `Current` by sequence alone (`resolve.rs:357`), so one create is silently lost. The issue's "Expected" says the read-back must classify a same-sequence different-bytes record as a lost race; the PR meets that for one endpoint order only, and `net.rs` tests only that order.
Fix: let the confirm see every endpoint answer. Smallest form: in `fanout_get_under` track `contested: bool` (a verified record at the best sequence with different bytes was seen) and expose it through a confirm-only `fanout_get_contested(...) -> Option<(VerifiedRecord, Vec<u8>, bool)>`; then in `publish.rs`:

```rust
Some((_, bytes, contested)) if bytes == record_bytes && !contested => PublishOutcome::Published { sequence },
Some((observed, _, _)) if observed.sequence >= sequence => PublishOutcome::LostRace { .. },
```

Add `publish_confirm_reads_a_sibling_on_a_later_endpoint_as_a_lost_race` (mirror of the new `net.rs` test, sibling seeded on endpoint 1 only). Both racing devices then halt, the next read leg adopts the tie winner, and each rebases and signs above.

### F2 — should-fix — CONFIRMED — `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:5753`

Defect: the pre-signature re-resolve runs only for the scope root; interior folders share the same name derivation (`write_name` drain.rs:794, `write_name_signer` session.rs:205) and the same stale-base window.
Failure scenario: `ensure_folder` loads an interior folder once per pass and returns early on `pass.holds(folder)` (drain.rs:2397); uploads run between that load and the signature. Device B loads F at n and uploads for minutes; device A creates a child in F and confirms F at n+1; B signs n+1 over a body without A's child. Under F1's endpoint order B's confirm is `Published` and A's create is lost with no error. The issue's "Expected" is written for "a publish", not only a root.
Fix: generalise `reresolve_scope_root` to `reresolve_before_signing(plane, folder, built_on)`: root uses `root_adopter`; an interior folder builds the `ChildAdopter` exactly as `load_child_node` does (drain.rs:2305-2313) and runs the same `resolve_gated(NoCache)` / `TrustViolation` / `> built_on` logic. Drop the `if is_scope_root` guard. Add a `write_plane` test with two devices writing one interior folder mid-pass. If the orchestrator keeps the PR root-scoped, file the interior case as a follow-up with a dependency edge before merge; the blueprint sweep needs only the root.

### F3 — should-fix — CONFIRMED — `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:5814` and the `Halt::Attempt` doc `:391-397`

Defect: a pre-signature lost race is charged against `ATTEMPT_BUDGET` (5, then `AttemptsExhausted` dead-letter, drain.rs:1918-1935), but the budget's own rule (`:571-575`, "spent only by a halt the valve could attribute to these bytes") and the `Attempt` doc's reason ("a retry re-signs at the same sequence") do not hold here: nothing was PUT, the adopt raised the floor, the retry signs higher.
Failure scenario: device A drains a batch of creates (one root publish per create); device B has a create with a long upload at its head. Each B pass re-resolves after its upload, sees A's newer root, halts `Attempt`. Charges are durable and never decay while the op stays queued. After five losses B's create is dead-lettered although it was never refused. Four independent reads (altitude, crypto, spec, standards) reached the same conclusion.
Fix: charge it to the unattributed budget — return `Halt::Unclassified` at drain.rs:5814 with a one-line reason, or add `Halt::LostRace` handled next to `Unclassified` in `apply_valve` (charge_unattributed, no name handed back, same `upload_failure` text as `Attempt`). Restore the original `Attempt` doc. Add a test asserting the attempt count stays 0 after a pre-signature lost race.

### F4 — should-fix — CONFIRMED — `blueprint/engine.md:927-930`

Defect: "…the two-device publish fix — re-resolve, then sign above the highest sequence seen — which is not landed; without it two owner devices … publish two records at one sequence." This PR lands that fix for the scope root the sweep writes. The clause is a status marker in the exact form AGENTS.md "Tracker references" prescribes, and that rule says it "stops being true in the same diff that falsifies it". No design statement changes, so no ADR is needed.
Fix (in this PR): keep the dependency, drop the status clause: "The sweep depends on the two-device publish fix — the drain re-resolves the root through the gate just before it signs and signs above the highest sequence it observed, and a confirm that reads a sibling's record at its own sequence is a lost race the next pass rebases and signs above."

### F5 — nit — simplify patch at `~/.claude/scratch/w1963/C/review/simplify.patch` (110 lines; builds, tests green, clippy clean; tree restored)

Hunks: (a) `drain.rs` — extract `gated_scope_root(scope, end, mode) -> Result<GatedResolve, Halt>`; `resolve_scope_root` and `reresolve_scope_root` both call it; the redundant `name` parameter is removed (`end.root_name` is the same value, drain.rs:2220); (b) `reresolve_scope_root` doc cut to five lines with the blueprint citation, no happy-path narration; (c) `publish.rs:380-382` confirm comment cut to one sentence. ### F6 — nit — CONFIRMED — `crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:5799-5809` (cost)

Every root publish adds one sequential fan-out GET (E endpoints) plus, on the usual equal-floor `Current` path, a gateway head-block fetch and unseal (`adopter.rs` `recover_own_scope_material` → `fetch_head_block`; the fresh `root_adopter` holds no local head). - `resolve.rs:357`: a record at exactly the floor is `Current` by sequence alone; a sibling's different bytes at the floor are never a conflict. Deepest home of the single-writer assumption (store the floor record hash beside the floor).

Title: parentheses only in the scope. Body: bare `Closes #1959.`, no attribution, "fails without the fix" claims verified true. One overstatement: "reads another record at our own sequence as `LostRace`" holds only when the fan-out picks the sibling's record (F1).

**Files analyzed:** 37 (diff) plus the source of every touched path
**Crypto operations touched:** ECDSA preimages (grant-set commitment, recipient binding), unkeyed BLAKE3 fingerprint, re-seal and re-mint producers
**Issues found:** 0 critical, 2 high, 1 medium, 2 low

### Findings

#### [HIGH] The write wave re-signs a committed link entry as a perpetual personal grant

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:4308-4321` (`remint_grants`), `crates/engine/src/grants/ledger.rs:156-192` (`mint_grant_row`)

`remint_grants` builds the re-minted entry with `mint_grant_row`, which calls `GrantSetEntry::new` (always `Personal`, no `deadline`, no `admission_cap`, no `conversion_permission`), then copies only `unknown` from `committed_entry`. The row comes from `mint_grant_row` too, so `via_link` and `grantee_name` are gone and the row is owner-signed without them.

Scenario: the decoder now accepts a link entry, so a record authored by the mint slice (or any newer build) holds `{kind: link, deadline, admissionCap}` at `read`. The owner revokes an unrelated write grantee, which runs a write wave. The wave re-mints the link entry as a personal `read` entry with no deadline and no cap, and the owner signs it. The link holder keeps reading past the deadline for ever, the cap is unenforceable, and every converted row loses the `viaLink` that ADR 0023 D9 counts. This is fail-open on the field this PR introduces, in a function this PR edits, so it belongs in this PR, not the rotation slice.

Fix: carry every owner-signed field by struct update, and re-sign the row with the carried fields:

```rust
let commitment_entry = GrantSetEntry {
    tag: minted.commitment_entry.tag,
    masked_recipient_enc_pk: minted.commitment_entry.masked_recipient_enc_pk,
    pseudonym_pk: minted.commitment_entry.pseudonym_pk,
    ..committed_entry.clone()   // kind, deadline, conversion_permission, admission_cap, unknown
};
let mut ledger_entry = minted.ledger_entry;
if row_is_owner_attested(&owner_identity, row, old_name) {
    ledger_entry.via_link = row.via_link.map(|t| new_tag_of[&t]);   // old tag -> re-minted tag (ADR 0023 D2)
    ledger_entry.grantee_name = row.grantee_name.clone();
    ledger_entry.owner_sig = sign_recipient_binding(self.owner, new_name, &ledger_entry).to_compact();
}
```

The old-to-new tag map is available from the same loop. An unattested row's name and via-link are a write grantee's to choose, so they follow `recipient_identity_pk` and drop.

#### [HIGH] The re-seal budget is sized for a 224-byte row and copies writer-authored names of up to 565 bytes

**Location:** `crates/engine/src/content/limits.rs:42`, `crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:836,1052-1058,1104`, `crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal/tests.rs:870-941`

A bare row measures 234 bytes on the wire (`a5` map, keys, 64+32+33+32 bytes, `"read"`), already over `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES = 224`. A row with `viaLink` + a 255-byte `granteeName` + `nameSource: "claimant"` measures 565. `reseal_scope_root` runs `enforce_committed_ledger` only (tag + permission, line 836) and then copies `via_link` and `grantee_name` from every committed row verbatim (1055-1056) with no `row_is_owner_attested` check. `resealable_section_bytes(1024)` = 909,312. Measured from the KAT vectors, a maximal bare re-seal is about 675 KB (read blob 281, row 234, child ref 98, history link 181 per item); full-width rows add 341 x 1024 = 349 KB, to about 1,024 KB, over the budget by about 115 KB. The break-even is about 750 committed rows.

Scenario: a committed write grantee on a scope with 750 or more committed grants re-authors the write body with a 255-byte name and `nameSource` on every row (no signature needed: the re-seal never checks one). The owner's next revoke hits `SectionNotResealable` (`reseal.rs:1104`), which `net/rotation.rs:3828` maps to `NotLanded`, on every retry. The scope is rotation-proof and the writer is un-revocable. The maximal test at `reseal/tests.rs:870` uses `attested_row` bare rows with a padded unknown map the re-seal drops, so it cannot see this.

Fix, both halves: (1) set `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES` to the full-width row derived from the constants (`234 + 42 + (14 + MAX_GRANTEE_NAME_BYTES) + 20`, rounded to 576) so an honest owner with 1024 named grantees can still rotate; (2) carry `via_link` and `grantee_name` only when `row_is_owner_attested`, which removes the writer lever entirely. Rebuild the maximal test with full-width rows.

#### [MEDIUM] `GranteeName` admits bidi overrides and zero-width characters in an owner-signed name shown beside the fingerprint

**Location:** `crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:135-141`; engine law at `crates/engine/src/name.rs:92-105`

`char::is_control` covers Cc only. U+202E, U+2066-2069, U+200B, U+FEFF, U+2028 are Cf/Zl and pass. The engine already refuses exactly this set for node names (`validate_name`, `NameError::DeceptiveCharacter`) and strips it at render, but core cannot import that set, and the claim name will be validated by the codec every build shares.

Scenario: a claimant suggests `"Alice\u{202E}renwo"`. Conversion copies it into a row the owner signs with flag `claimant`; the people table and every co-writer render "Alice" with "owner" drawn reversed beside the fingerprint; a line separator (U+2028) fakes a second confirmation line, which is the exact case the control-character KAT vector says it closes.

Fix: move the `is_deceptive` character set into core (a small `crates/core/src/name.rs`, or beside `GranteeName`), have `GranteeName::new` refuse it with `invalid-grantee-name`, add a reject KAT vector, and have `crates/engine/src/name.rs` use the core set so the law has one home.

#### [LOW] A link entry needs no deadline and no admission cap

**Location:** `crates/core/src/seal/grant.rs:898-916` (`validate`)

`validate` refuses link fields on a personal entry and a non-`read` link, and nothing else. A `{kind: link}` entry with no `deadline` and no `admissionCap` encodes, signs and decodes. CONTEXT.md "Link entry" says it carries all three. Scenario: the conversion slice reads `admission_cap: None` as unlimited, which is the 1024-row enrolment ADR 0023 D9 exists to stop. Either require both on `Link` in `validate` (fail-closed, one more reject vector) or write the absent-cap rule now (absent = zero admissions).

#### [LOW] `expiresAt: 0` now decodes

The `ledger-zero-expiry` reject vector is gone; a row carrying `expiresAt: 0` decodes as a preserved unknown and re-encodes byte-stable. Acceptable under the retirement and no engine path reads it (checked below). Note only.

Fix both, reply inside each thread and resolve it through GraphQL, post one disposition comment, and make ONE push. Do not request a CodeRabbit review. Every `gh` call prefixed `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh`. No attribution lines.

Thread 1 (`crates/engine/src/net/publish.rs:389`, "First-endpoint tie remains split"): when our record sits on the first endpoint and a sibling's different record on another endpoint at the same sequence, the confirm now reports `LostRace`. On the retry a normal resolve picks our bytes (first endpoint wins the tie), the drain sees the create as already satisfied, drops the op, and never publishes a higher record. The other endpoint keeps the sibling's record. Fix: on a contested confirm, adopt the SIBLING's record (the contested bytes), not ours, so the retry rebases onto the sibling's record and signs strictly above it with our op included. Make the contested fan-out variant return the contested record for this purpose. Add a test: our bytes on endpoint 0, the sibling's on endpoint 1, both at S; after the retry every endpoint holds one record at S+1 that contains both creates.

Thread 2 (`crates/engine/src/sync/drain.rs:5824`, "Equal sequences can hide changes"): the pre-signature check compares only the sequence. When the pass built the folder from cached bytes and the fresh gated resolve returns different bytes at the same sequence, the drain signs the old folder body and the higher record erases the sibling's change. Fix: compare the fresh record's bytes (or a hash of the record) with the bytes the pass built on; equal sequence with different bytes is a lost race: adopt the fresh record, halt `LostRace`, rebase on the next pass. Add a test: the cache holds record X at S, endpoint 0 holds a different record Y at S, the pass halts, and the next pass signs S+1 over Y with the op applied.

Keep the reader-side residual (a resolve at exactly the floor cannot tell two records apart) out of this PR; it is filed as issue 1984. Say so in the thread replies where it applies.

Then run `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine`, `cargo test --workspace --exclude fuser`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy with `-D warnings`, the wasm32 check, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`. Update the PR body list of changes and tests through the REST API. Wait for CI green with one polling script. Report the new head SHA.

# Review of PR #1983 — feat(core): link fields, named ledger row, key fingerprint

Head `ae60628392c00fec9095090b9b69270c038ba2be`, branch `feat/1963-core-link-fields`. CI: every check green at head. PR body: no attribution, bare `Closes #N.` lines, title parentheses hold the scope only.

## Findings (by severity)

### should-fix 1 — the re-seal budget does not count the new row fields
- `crates/engine/src/content/limits.rs:42` (`LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES = 224`) with `crates/engine/src/rotation/reseal.rs:1055-1056`.
- Defect: `reseal_scope_root` now copies `via_link` and `grantee_name` from every committed row. The per-row budget still describes the old row. Measured from the KAT bytes: a bare row is 234 bytes, a linked row with a short name is 314-319 bytes, a row with a 255-byte name is about 565 bytes.
- Failure scenario: `enforce_committed_ledger` compares only `(tag, permission)`, and the re-seal never checks the row owner signature. A committed write grantee puts a 255-byte `granteeName` on every row. The minted section exceeds `resealable_section_bytes` (reseal.rs:1102) and the re-seal returns `SectionNotResealable`. The scope becomes rotation-proof. The maximal re-seal test (`reseal/tests.rs:874-941`) uses bare rows, so nothing catches it.
- Fix: derive the per-row budget from core constants (`234 + 42 + MAX_GRANTEE_NAME_BYTES + ~34`) with a compile-time assert, and extend the maximal re-seal test to rows with `via_link` and a 255-byte name. Alternative: carry `grantee_name` only when `row_is_owner_attested` passes.

### should-fix 2 — the write-wave re-mint drops every new owner-signed field
- `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:4313-4321` (`remint_grants`).
- Defect: the re-minted entry comes from `GrantSetEntry::new` (always `Personal`); only `unknown` is copied from `committed_entry`. `kind`, `deadline`, `conversion_permission`, `admission_cap` are lost and the owner re-signs a personal entry. The row loses `via_link` and `grantee_name`.
- Failure scenario: an owner device on this build re-mints a record that another build wrote with a link entry. The link loses its deadline and cap; its admitted rows lose the via-link reference. This fails open. No producer mints a link entry yet, but the decoder already accepts one.
- Spec note: #1965 defers only the via-link re-map; #1973 names only the re-map. The loss of the entry link fields and the grantee name is a silent gap.
- Fix: `GrantSetEntry { tag, masked_recipient_enc_pk, ..committed_entry.clone() }` (keep the pseudonym check) so every owner-signed field carries by default; carry `grantee_name` when `row_is_owner_attested` passes; until the tag re-map lands, carry `via_link` unchanged or return `Rejected` for a row that has one, and state the re-map in #1973.

### nit 3 — absence-justifying comment
- `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs:751-753`: "Nothing in a resolved record this build mints marks a row as an invite". This diff adds `EntryKind::Link` and `viaLink`; the sentence turns false when a link entry mints. Replace with: "`links` is the owner's own record of the live links on this scope; a claim converts only against one of those."

### nit 4 — absence-justifying comment
- `crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:599-601`: "The decoder's grantee-name rejects need no guard here …". Delete; the rule lives on the `GranteeName` doc (line 114).

### nit 5 — grantee-name policy admits deceptive characters
- `crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:136-140`: `GranteeName::new` refuses only `char::is_control`. Bidi overrides/isolates, zero-width characters, U+2028/2029 pass; `crates/engine/src/name.rs:92 is_deceptive` refuses them for node names. The length bound matches ADR 0027 D1 (255 = `MAX_NODE_NAME_BYTES`). Not exploitable here: no engine path builds a name and no UI shows one. Fix: move `is_deceptive` into core and call it from `GranteeName::new`, now or in the claim slice.

### nit 6 — duplicated helpers and dead code (from `/simplify`, verified)
- `kat_gen.rs:7667-7680` `entry_with`: the `retain` loop is dead (`Map::insert` replaces); base pairs repeat `grant_set_entry_map`. Same at `kat_gen.rs:5940` `named_entry` vs `good_entry()`.
- `kat_gen.rs:5753` `named_ledger_row` repeats `signed_ledger_row`; `write_body.rs:1237` `named_row` repeats `signed_row`. Share one `sign(entry)` step.
- `kat_manifest.rs:4440-4444` `binding_row` inlines the `"claimant"|"owner"` match a third time. Add `NameSource::from_wire(&str) -> Option<Self>` and use it in `from_value` and the test.
- `grant.rs:2270` and `write_body.rs:1389` repeat tests in `tests/encode_refusals.rs`; keep the release-run copies.
- `grant.rs:900` `GrantSetEntry::validate` is `pub` with no external caller.
- `packages/client/src/testkit.ts:532` `fingerprintKeys` is written and never read.
- `invite.rs:1411` the `mint` closure repeats the `link()` helper (1645).

## Gate verdicts

- `/simplify`: four agents ran read-only; no edit applied, so no patch exists under `~/.claude/scratch/w1963/A/review/`. Findings folded into nit 6 and should-fix 1-2.
- `/security-review`: no finding above 0.7 confidence. Preimage is one canonical det-CBOR map; a lone `granteeName`/`nameSource` is `missing-field`; every signer and verifier routes through `encode_grant_set_commitment`, so `validate` is release-active; `from_sec1` refuses non-33-byte input; Debug impls redact; no engine path reads a row deadline. The latent gap it noted is should-fix 2.
- `/crypto-privacy-review`: the dedicated reviewer reported to the orchestrator directly; its result did not return to this context. My own checks on its axes: preimage unambiguous; pre-change vectors byte-stable (`invite-expiring-entry` unchanged); removal of a present signed field fails `identity-signature-invalid`, class `trust`; fingerprint 80 bits, fixed encoding, KAT pinned, browser suite asserts the same strings; store kind 0x03 reserved; encode refusals run under `--release` inside "Core KATs (native + WASM)"; no secret bytes in assertions.
- `/code-review` (standards + spec): both agents reported to the orchestrator directly; results did not return here. Own spec check: #1964 and #1966 complete; #1965 complete except the silent re-mint gap (should-fix 2). Own standards check: nits 3-4; no tracker refs; terminology matches `CONTEXT.md`.

input.message:
The reviewers of PR 1983 confirmed the findings below. Apply all of them, commit, and make ONE push. Then wait for CI green with one polling script and report. Do not mark the PR ready and do not request a review. Lane D builds on your branch (`feat/1963-engine-link-mint-read`, stacked on yours), so keep the wire names and public signatures you already exposed stable where you can, and list every renamed or re-typed public item in your report.

SHOULD-FIX 1: the write-wave re-mint drops every new owner-signed field. `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:4308-4321` `remint_grants` builds the entry with `mint_grant_row` → `GrantSetEntry::new` (always personal) and copies only `unknown`. Fix: build the re-minted entry by struct update so `kind`, `deadline`, `conversion_permission`, `admission_cap` and `unknown` carry from `committed_entry` (keep the pseudonym check). For the row: when `row_is_owner_attested` passes, carry `grantee_name` and the name source, re-map `via_link` from the old tag to the re-minted tag (the old-to-new tag map is available in the same loop), and re-sign the row with `sign_recipient_binding` under the new name. An unattested row's name and via-link drop with its identity key. Tests in `net/rotation.rs`: the re-mint carries a link entry's four fields and `verify_grant_set` passes over the re-minted set; the re-mint re-maps an attested row's `via_link` to the link's new tag, carries the name, and the new row verifies under the new name; an unattested row's name drops.

SHOULD-FIX 2: the re-seal budget is sized for a bare row. `crates/engine/src/content/limits.rs:42` `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES = 224`, but a bare row measures 234 bytes on the wire and a row with `viaLink`, a 255-byte `granteeName` and `nameSource` measures about 565. `reseal_scope_root` (`rotation/reseal.rs:1052-1058`) copies `via_link` and `grantee_name` from every committed row with no owner-signature check, so a committed write grantee can put a 255-byte name on every row of a scope with about 750 grants and make every revoke fail with `SectionNotResealable`. Fix both halves: derive `LEDGER_ROW_WIRE_BYTES` from the constants (`234 + 42 + (14 + MAX_GRANTEE_NAME_BYTES) + 20`, rounded up to 576) with a test or const assert that pins the measured maximal row; and carry `via_link` and `grantee_name` only when `row_is_owner_attested` passes. Rebuild the maximal re-seal test (`rotation/reseal/tests.rs:870-941`) with full-width rows so it fits inside `resealable_section_bytes(MAX_GRANT_BLOBS)`; add a test that a name on a row whose owner signature does not verify is not carried.

SHOULD-FIX 3: `GranteeName::new` (`crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:135-141`) refuses only `char::is_control` (Cc). Bidi overrides and isolates (U+202A-202E, U+2066-2069), zero-width characters (U+200B-200D, U+2060, U+FEFF) and U+2028/2029 pass. The engine already refuses that set for node names in `crates/engine/src/name.rs:92-105` `is_deceptive`. Fix: move the deceptive-character set into core (a small module beside `GranteeName` or `crates/core/src/name.rs`), make `GranteeName::new` and the decoder refuse it with `invalid-grantee-name`, add a reject KAT vector, and make the engine `name.rs` use the core set so the law has one home. Add release-run cases in `encode_refusals.rs` for U+202E, U+2066, U+200B, U+FEFF, U+2028.

SHOULD-FIX 4: a `{kind: link}` entry with no `deadline` or no `admissionCap` encodes and decodes. Read CONTEXT.md "link entry" and ADR 0023 D9: require on a link entry every field CONTEXT.md says it carries, in `validate`, on decode and encode, with one reject vector per missing field and a release-run case. A cap of zero stays accepted.

NIT 5: absence-justifying comments. `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs:750-752` ("Nothing in a resolved record this build mints marks a row as an invite") and the same shape at `invite.rs:307`: replace with what the code does, for example "`links` is the owner's own record of the live links on this scope; a claim converts only against one of those." `crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:599-601` ("The decoder's grantee-name rejects need no guard here"): delete the sentence.

NIT 6: rationale restated three times: keep the CI-step comment in `.github/workflows/ci-rust.yml`; drop the copies in `crates/core/tests/encode_refusals.rs:1-3` and the `grant.rs` test doc.

NIT 7: terminology and types. Rename the check id `invalid-expiry` on the commitment entry to `invalid-deadline` (CONTEXT.md names the concept "deadline"; the ledger row check is retired). `invite.rs:356` hand-checks `deadline.0 == 0` on `UnixMillis` while core types the deadline as `NonZeroU64`; use the typed value. Rename the `seal` re-export `EntryKind` to `GrantSetEntryKind` if the rename is contained; skip it and say so if it spreads wide.

NIT 8: duplicates and dead code. `kat_gen.rs:7667-7680` `entry_with` has a dead `retain` loop (`Map::insert` replaces) and repeats `grant_set_entry_map`; `kat_gen.rs:5940` `named_entry` repeats `good_entry()`; `kat_gen.rs:5753` `named_ledger_row` repeats `signed_ledger_row`; `write_body.rs:1237` `named_row` repeats `signed_row`: share one sign step. `kat_manifest.rs:4440-4444` `binding_row` inlines the `"claimant"|"owner"` match a third time: add `NameSource::from_wire(&str) -> Option<Self>` and use it in `from_value` and the test; also replace the positional `binding_row(name, [&String; 3], [&Option<String>; 3], signature)` signature with the vector struct. `grant.rs:2270` and `write_body.rs:1389` repeat the tests in `tests/encode_refusals.rs`: keep only the release-run copies. `grant.rs:900` `GrantSetEntry::validate` is `pub` with no external caller: make it private. `packages/client/src/testkit.ts:532` `fingerprintKeys` is never read: delete. `invite.rs:1411` the `mint` closure repeats the `link()` helper at 1645: use the helper. `packages/client/test/browser/boundary.worker.ts:55-65` hand-copies `fingerprint.json`: import the vector file instead. `crates/engine/src/grants/contact.rs` test module: put the `use` lines before `#[test]`.

NIT 9: KAT coverage. Add one accept vector per link field on its own (not only the all-fields vector), reject vectors that pin `commitment-invalid` when `kind`, `conversionPermission` or `admissionCap` is edited after signing, a vector with `conversionPermission` on a personal entry, an unknown `kind`, `kind: 1` and `deadline: "soon"` as `unexpected-type`, `admissionCap: 0` on a link accepted. In `write_body.rs` unit tests: a 253-byte ASCII name plus one 2-byte char (255 bytes) accepted and 254 plus one 2-byte char (256) refused; swapping the `granteeName` and `nameSource` values yields distinct preimages.

Keep the explicit `kind: "personal"` refusal as it is (canonical form).

Run `cargo test -p cipherbox-core`, `cargo test --workspace --exclude fuser`, the release run of `encode_refusals`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy with `-D warnings`, the wasm32 check, `pnpm install`, the client unit and browser suites, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`. Regenerate the KAT vectors with `kat_gen`. Update the PR body through the REST API (`gh api -X PATCH repos/FSM1/cipher-box/pulls/1983 -F body=@file`) so it lists the re-mint carry, the budget, the deceptive-character rule and the new vectors; keep the three bare `Closes` lines and no attribution. Check `git log --format=%B origin/main..HEAD | grep -i "co-authored\|generated with"` prints nothing. Report the new head SHA, CI status, and the list of renamed or re-typed public items.

# #1969 engine: the claim carries the scope pointer name and re-posts until the deadline

The claim posts the scope pointer name with the contact code and the name. The engine re-posts the claim with one idempotency key until the deadline.

## Decisions

- [ADR 0023](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0023-the-invite-link-is-the-primary-sharing-path-and-conversion-runs-by-itself.md) D3, D6
- [ADR 0027](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0027-a-grantee-name-is-not-an-identity.md) D1

## Scope

- The claim payload is `{claimId, scopePointerName, contactCode, name}`.
- Each claim has one idempotency key. Every re-post uses the same key.
- Re-posts use exponential backoff. They stop at the deadline.
- A second claim of the same link on one device is a no-op. It is not a gate failure.
- The name is the sign-in display name by default. When there is no display name, the name is empty. The name is never the email.

## Acceptance

- Two posts of one claim carry one key.
- No post occurs after the deadline.
- A second claim command returns the existing state.
- Gate: the Rust gate (Workspace tests) blocks the merge.

## Files

- `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs` (claim)
- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` claim command
- `crates/engine/src/api/client.rs`

## Batch

PR batch C with #1976 and #1970.

## Depends on

Part of #1963.

# #1970 engine: conversion runs on the tick and on dialog open, ack first

Any owner device converts claims on every tick and when the share dialog opens. The device acks the mailbox item first. It converts only when the API answers "removed". There is no approve step.

## Decisions

- [ADR 0023](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0023-the-invite-link-is-the-primary-sharing-path-and-conversion-runs-by-itself.md) D3, D4, D5, D6, D7, D9
- [ADR 0024](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0024-a-link-holder-reads-at-once-from-the-link-blob.md) D4
- [ADR 0026](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0026-a-scope-root-takes-many-grants.md) C5, E1
- [ADR 0027](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0027-a-grantee-name-is-not-an-identity.md) D3

## Scope

- On every tick and on share-dialog open, any owner device opens the claim items.
- The device acks first. It converts only when the API answers "removed".
- Run the D3 checks: the link entry is live; the kind is link; the deadline verdict; the contact code binding; the admission cap.
- The device computes the deadline verdict once, at the ack, against the injected `now`. It stores the verdict in the op entry.
- The admission cap counts the live rows that have the via-link reference. It does not count the owner.
- When the identity already has a row, conversion is a no-op. It never changes an existing row.
- Conversion appends the personal row at the conversion permission, with the via-link reference, the grantee name and the source `claimant`.
- For a write link, conversion mints the write material. When the folder has no write scope, it runs a write-scope cut first.
- The engine publishes one root per folder per tick.
- Conversion is a durable op entry. Its retry covers the full conversion.
- A refusal at the 1024-row cap dead-letters the entry. It does not block the queue.
- The engine never cuts a link that has a pending op entry.
- The converting device shows one transient "joined" notice.
- The people list updates on every owner device from the record.

## Acceptance

- A claim from device A converts on device B.
- A "not removed" answer converts nothing.
- A write conversion on a read-only folder runs one write-scope cut.
- A link with a full cap refuses the conversion.
- A second claim by the same identity appends no row.
- After a transient failure, the retry runs the checks again.
- Gate: the Rust gate (Workspace tests) blocks the merge.

## Files

- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` `convert_invite_claims`
- `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs` convert
- `ops` queue
- `crates/engine/src/api/client.rs` mailbox DELETE

## Batch

PR batch C with #1976 and #1969.

## Depends on

Part of #1963.

# #1971 engine: a grant or a link on a shared folder appends a row
When a folder already names a scope, a direct grant and a link mint append a row to the ledger. They do not make a new seed. The owner can edit a grantee name.
## Decisions
- [ADR 0026](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0026-a-scope-root-takes-many-grants.md) D1-D7, C5
- [ADR 0027](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0027-a-grantee-name-is-not-an-identity.md) D4, D6
## Scope
- When the folder already names a scope, the direct grant and the link mint use the append path: append a row, sign again, publish once. There is no new seed and no re-seal of the subtree.
- Retire the `grant-target-already-names-a-scope` refusal for this case.
- A grant to an existing grantee with a different permission calls the permission change (E6). With the same permission, it answers already-has-access.
- A folder can have any number of live links.
- Nested scopes do not change.
- The owner edits a grantee name in the people list. This is a row update with source `owner` and one root publish.
- Each device keeps a contact-book cache of names by identity for pre-fill. The cache is never synced.
## Acceptance
- A second grant appends a row and publishes once.
- The retired refusal does not occur.
- A name edit changes only the name and the flag of that row.
- Gate: the Rust gate (Workspace tests) blocks the merge.
## Files
- `crates/engine/src/grants/create.rs`
- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`
- `seams` (contact-book cache)
## Batch
PR batch D with #1972.
## Depends on
Part of #1963.
# #1972 engine: a grantee's permission can change
The owner can change the permission of a grantee. An upgrade mints write material. A downgrade is a write revoke that keeps the read row. The permission of a link does not change.
## Decisions
- [ADR 0025](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0025-revocation-under-the-link-first-model.md) D6
- [ADR 0026](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0026-a-scope-root-takes-many-grants.md) D4
## Scope
- An upgrade from read to write mints the write material. When the folder has no write scope, it runs a write-scope cut first.
- A downgrade from write to read is a write revoke. It keeps the read row.
- The permission of a link is fixed.
## Acceptance
- An upgrade on a read-only folder runs one write-scope cut, and the grantee can write.
- A downgrade runs the write cut, and the grantee can still read.
- Gate: the Rust gate (Workspace tests) blocks the merge.
## Files
- `crates/engine/src/facade.rs`
- `crates/engine/src/rotation/trigger.rs`
## Batch
PR batch D with #1971.
## Depends on
Part of #1963.

cat > ~/.claude/scratch/w1963/D/fold.md <<'EOF'
# Fold brief for PR 1986 (lane D) — apply all, ONE commit, ONE push

## Step 0 — rebase onto the moved base
Batch A pushed head 39e0dfcf3 on `feat/1963-core-link-fields`. Run `git fetch origin && git rebase origin/feat/1963-core-link-fields`. Public items changed there: `EntryKind` → `GrantSetEntryKind`; `Malformed::InvalidExpiry` → `InvalidDeadline` (check id `invalid-deadline`); `GrantSetEntry::validate` is private; new `NameSource::from_wire`, `cipherbox_core::name::is_deceptive`; a link entry MUST set `deadline`, `conversion_permission` and `admission_cap` or encoding fails; `remint_grants` in `net/rotation.rs` now carries every owner-signed entry field, re-maps `via_link` and re-signs attested rows (drop your own copy-back hunk at `rotation.rs:4319-4325` in favour of the base's code; if the base does it by hand, add `GrantSetEntry::rebound(&self, fresh) -> GrantSetEntry` in core that keeps every field of `self` and takes only `tag` and the masked recipient key from `fresh`, and use it).

## Should-fix (security and correctness)
S1. Join order (crypto L2 + spec "deadline at join"). In `claim_invite_link` run the pointer consult FIRST under the fragment's pointer name, read key and the imported owner identity. A `Rejected` consult is a TrustViolation: no claim post, no contact-book record, no bookmark. Then try one read of the root: when it succeeds, check the link entry is live and its deadline is not reached; an expired or revoked link posts no claim and answers the expired/revoked state. When the consult or the read is only unavailable, post the claim, bookmark, and let the tick retry (the first read never fails the claim command). Tests: a forged contact code in the fragment posts no claim and records no contact; a join of an expired link posts no claim; an unavailable pointer still posts and bookmarks.
S2. (link-read 1) Drop `linkSecret` only after the personal blob OPENS: push `HoldChange::Drop` only when `open` returns `Ok(Some(_))` on the personal path, never on the `Granted` class alone. Test: a personal blob that fails to open keeps the link keys.
S3. (link-read 2) The refresh is a load-modify-persist writer of the received-shares list across network awaits, and the claim command writes the same list. Load the list again just before the persist and apply the heal, deadline and drop changes by key (or serialize every writer through one engine async lock). Test: a join during a pass is not lost.
S4. (link-read 3) On the link path never render a record under a root name this pass did not vouch through the pointer. When the consult is unavailable, keep the previous classification and render nothing new; when the pointer is absent (`Ok(None)`), classify Unresolvable. Test: a pointer that goes unavailable after a wave does not render the old root.
S5. (link-read 4 + spec) Add an `owner_actions` test: mint a link, join, run a REAL write wave, the holder is still `Granted`, the entry is still a link with the same deadline, and the holder reads through the moved root.
S6. (crypto L3) `MalformedFragment` gets the class `malformed`, the same as a malformed claim.
S7. (crypto L1) Add accept KAT vectors that pin the fragment bytes (the claim vector belongs to the claim slice). Add a release-run encode refusal for an oversize contact code in the fragment (2048-byte bound).
S8. (standards silent fallback) `received_status.rs:717` `EphemeralInvitee::from_secret(..).ok()` drops an invalid stored secret silently. Classify that share Unresolvable and emit nothing else; do not skip it silently.
S9. (crypto M1, M2 — state, do not build) The spent set is gone, so the mailbox server can replay a converted claim after a revoke until ack-first lands, and the admission cap is signed but not enforced until conversion writes `viaLink` rows. Both are the claim/conversion slice, which lands next in this stack. State both windows in the PR body under "Known windows closed by the next slice". Also state: conversion now always mints `read`, so a write link gives read until that slice lands; and the bookmark carries three optional keys (`linkSecret`, `scopePointerName`, `linkDeadline`) where ADR 0024 D1 says one; the orchestrator files the ADR note.

## Simplification (apply)
P1. `facade.rs:559` `invite_links: Option<SharingInviteLinks>` is always `Some`: make it non-optional through wasm (`invite_links` getter), `protocol.ts:263`, `sharing.store.ts:47`, `commandCodec.ts:933`; delete the web `unavailable` state (`inviteLink.ts:57-63`, `InviteLinkPanel.tsx:38`), `NoLocalLink` (`InviteLinkPanel.tsx:123-131`, its text is false now) and their tests. Fix the stale "link records" doc text at `facade.rs:3358`, `wasm/src/lib.rs:733-734`, `protocol.ts:246`, `protocol.ts:263`, `sharing.store.ts:47`, `inviteLink.ts:57` and the UI copy "claims convert on the browser that made the link".
P2. One expiry predicate at one home: `UnixMillis::reached(self, deadline: Option<UnixMillis>) -> bool` (or `deadline_passed`) used by `LinkHold::is_expired`, `CommittedLink::is_expired`, `received_status.rs:761` and `rotation/trigger.rs:627`. Decide the `Expired` class once in the refresh loop after `classified` (a fresh deadline read this pass wins over the stored one); `Classified::unresolvable` takes no parameters.
P3. `received_status.rs:283` replace `link_deadline: Option<Option<UnixMillis>>` with `hold_change: Option<HoldChange>` computed at the tail of `classified`; the caller does `hold_changes.extend(hold_change)`. Add `ReceivedSharesList::set_link_deadline(&mut self, key, deadline)` and use it instead of cloning the hold (a needless copy of the secret). Drop the redundant `holds_changed = true` in the loop.
P4. Retire kind 0x03 by deleting the `InviteRecords` variant: `ALL` becomes 5 kinds; add `pub const RESERVED: &[(u8, &str)] = &[(0x03, "invite-records")]` and one test that no live kind reuses a reserved byte or name; the manifest pins `reserved`; remove the runtime `is_retired` refusal, `Malformed::RetiredOwnerLocalKind`, its check name, its reject vectors and its `encode_refusals` case (no encode path exists any more, so rule 8 does not apply). Keep the 20 cross-kind pairs and 10 family vectors.
P5. `rotation/trigger.rs:616-627` `prune_expired_grants` keeps a vestigial `owner_deadlines` parameter and has no production caller: delete the function and its tests (the sweep slice adds what it needs), or, if a production caller exists, remove the parameter and read `entry.deadline`.
P6. `invite.rs:507-531` `from_tree` and `accept.rs:614-617` `read_link_hold`: replace the hand wipe with `Zeroizing` and `?`.
P7. `accept.rs:229-237` delete the hand-written `Debug` for `LinkHold`; derive it (`SecretBytes` already redacts).
P8. `accept.rs:594-605` write the pair check as two `if`s and the deadline as `.map(..).transpose()?`.
P9. `facade.rs:9070` call `received.find(&key)` once; build `pending_link_bookmark` only when it is used (efficiency 3).
P10. `link_read.rs:34,55` store `""` as the display name when the names do not verify; the host renders "shared via link" when `viaLink && displayName === ''`. Add the test for the fallback at join.
P11. Keep `CommittedLink::conversion_permission` (the conversion slice reads it). Say so in one commit line, not in a comment.

## Reuse (apply)
R1. `sole_link(links) -> Option<&CommittedLink>` in `invite.rs`, used by `locate_invite_link` and the sharing read at `facade.rs:10689-10694` (delete the comment that says the rule is repeated).
R2. `block_on_while_ticking` in `testkit/executor.rs` exported from `testkit/mod.rs`; use it in `owner_actions.rs`, delete the local `command_while_ticking`.
R3. `invite_mint.rs:139` and `testkit/checks.rs:549`: use `cipherbox_core::suite::ecdsa::SIGNATURE_LEN` / `ECDSA_SIG_LEN`, not `64`.
R4. `invite_mint.rs:666-671` test: use `grants::self_locate_signed`.

## Efficiency (apply)
E1. `received_status.rs:610` `follow_held_pointers` shares `MAX_RESOLVES_PER_PASS` with the main loop, in the same list order (a forced pass otherwise resolves up to 1024 pointers).
E2. `facade.rs:9081` `claim_invite_link` files the forced pass without waiting on `pass.landed()`; the bookmark is already durable. Confirm that dropping the `ForcedPass` handle still runs the pass (`refresh.rs:129`). The host shows "claimed" before the listing updates; that is acceptable.
E3. (low) `convert_invite_claims` computes `committed_links` N+1 times; pass the list into `convert_invite_claim` and keep `authorise` per item. Optional; skip if the conversion slice rewrites the loop.

## Standards (apply)
T1. Absence-justifying comment at `invite.rs:824-825` ("A write grant needs the write material and a write-scope cut that this function does not run."): delete.
T2. The rule "a link entry is committed at read, no write-scope cut (ADR 0024 D4)" is stated at `invite.rs:14-16`, `invite.rs:287-288`, `invite_mint.rs:10-11`, `facade.rs:1191-1192`, `facade.rs:8441-8442`, `received_status.rs:490`: keep ONE citation at the mint, delete the rest. The ADR 0025 D5 `viaLink` note at `facade.rs:610`, `lib.rs:1226`, `protocol.ts:307`, `receivedShares.ts:49`: keep the Rust one and the TS type one.
T3. "fragment holder" → "link holder" at `invite.rs:610` and `invite.rs:718`. `facade.rs:8480` narration comment: delete.
T4. `packages/client/src/facade.ts:378`: `expiresAt?: bigint`, `ownerName = ''`; `useSharingActions.ts:107` passes no name; the comment cites ADR 0027 D5 (owner name in the fragment, source unstated) and says the D1 never-email rule applies by analogy. Keep the note once, at the facade default.

## Tests missing (add)
M1. A first read that fails and a later tick read that succeeds. M2. A facade-level join of an expired link. M3. A join of the same link twice on one device keeps the stored deadline (link-read nit 7).

## Run
`cargo test -p cipherbox-core`, `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine`, `cargo test --workspace --exclude fuser --exclude cipherbox-desktop`, both `kat_gen` runs with no drift, `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, the wasm32 check, `pnpm install`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, the `packages/client` and `apps/web` unit tests, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`. Update the PR body through the REST API: the changes, the tests and gates, the "Known windows closed by the next slice" section, the bookmark-key deviation, the two `Closes` lines, no attribution. Check `git log --format=%B origin/feat/1963-core-link-fields..HEAD | grep -i "co-authored\|generated with"` prints nothing. Report the new head SHA and every renamed or re-typed public item (lanes E and F build on your branch).
EOF

# #1973 engine: revocation under the link-first model
Link revoke and person revoke follow the link-first model. Any owner device can revoke. A re-commit on one device clears a stale local cut on another device.
## Decisions
- [ADR 0025](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0025-revocation-under-the-link-first-model.md) D1, D3, D4, D5
- [ADR 0024](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0024-a-link-holder-reads-at-once-from-the-link-blob.md) D3
- [ADR 0023](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0023-the-invite-link-is-the-primary-sharing-path-and-conversion-runs-by-itself.md) D2 (re-map)
## Scope
- A link revoke cuts the link holders at once. Grantees keep access, unless the owner ticks "also remove the N people who joined through it". The engine finds those rows by the via-link reference.
- A person revoke also cuts the link that admitted the person.
- Each revoke makes one cut set.
- The revoke derives the recipient key from the owner-signed ledger row. Thus any owner device can revoke.
- Cross-device rule: an owner-signed commitment that commits P again, at a cut epoch not below the cut this device recorded, clears the local cut for P on this device.
- A write wave re-mints every row at the new tag and re-maps each via-link reference.
- Cheap write rotation stays a hard requirement.
## Acceptance
- A link revoke without the checkbox keeps the grantees.
- A link revoke with the checkbox removes them in one cut.
- A person revoke cuts the admitting link in the same rotation.
- Device B stops withholding P after device A commits P again.
- After a write wave, the via-link references resolve to the new tags.
- Gate: the Rust gate (Workspace tests) blocks the merge.

- [ADR 0025](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0025-revocation-under-the-link-first-model.md) D2, E3

## Scope
- The sweep runs slower than the 30 s tick.

- It cuts each expired link, with one rotation per folder per sweep (batched).

## Acceptance
- The next sweep cuts an expired link on a device that never minted it.

# #1975 engine: a preview mode on the link path
A preview command runs the link read path and stores nothing and posts nothing. It returns the data for the invite page before join. Join is a separate command.

- [ADR 0028](https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box-next/blob/main/decisions/0028-the-invite-page-previews-before-join.md) D1-D7

- A preview leaves every seam store unchanged.

+            .any(|entry| entry.refused.is_none() && entry.claim.sender == claim.sender && entry.claim.payload == claim.payload)

input.message:
PR 1986 head bfe0fc496: Greptile 4/5 with one open thread, CodeRabbit one inline finding plus one outside-diff item. All three are valid. Fix them in ONE commit and ONE push, reply inside each thread and resolve it, post one disposition comment that also lists the outside-diff item, wait for CI green with one polling script, and report the new head. Do not request a review (a push to the ready PR re-triggers both bots by itself).

1. Greptile `facade.rs:8668` "Published link lacks owner setup": when the scope root publishes but the parent handover fails, the mint returns the fragment before it registers the new scope and saves its read seed, so the owner's own session may fail to read the folder or classify it as an owned scope until a later pass. Fix: register the scope and persist its read seed as soon as the root that commits the link lands, before the fragment returns; only the parent handover stays as the deferred work. Test: after a parent publish failure the owner session reads the folder as an owned scope on the next pass without a re-mint.
2. CodeRabbit inline `facade.rs:9256-9260`: `convert_invite_claim` can return `InviteError::GrantSetFull` and the fallback arm records it and breaks, so later claims in the same pass are never attempted, although a later claim can succeed and this one may become valid after a revoke. Fix: an explicit arm `Err(e @ InviteError::GrantSetFull)` that records the failure (`failure.get_or_insert(EngineError::from_invite(e))`) and continues; do not ack it.
3. CodeRabbit outside-diff `facade.rs:9273`: a claim that fails on `LinkExpired` can never convert (the deadline is owner-signed and no command extends it), yet the arm uses `continue`, so it is never acked, keeps an inbox slot until the mailbox TTL, and `pending_claim_counts` keeps counting it. Move `LinkExpired` to the ack arm; keep `LinkNotCommitted` and `ScopeMismatch` in the `continue` arm. Add a test that an expired-link claim is acked and no longer counted.

Note for the disposition: the claim/conversion slice (PR 1988) replaces this loop with ack-first conversion; these fixes keep this PR correct on its own.

- **Scenario:**
  - The owner revokes R' at scope S. The per-recipient floor and `cut_at = N` persist. The publish then fails: a crash, a `NotPublished` after the server took the PUT (lost ack), or a `LostRace`.
  - `record_cut_epoch_floor` never runs, so the device's cut-epoch floor stays N-1. The device re-adopts the N-1 set. A surviving write grantee can also republish it, which the gate accepts at floor N-1.
  - The owner then revokes X at S. `revoke_grants` signs cut epoch N and still commits R'. `effective_revoked_recipients` sees `N >= cut_at(N)`, raises `/cleared/` and serves R' a blob under the fresh seed.
  - Before this diff, R' stayed withheld. That was the "a crash between the two leaves the cut remembered" guarantee at `cascade.rs:728`, and this diff removes it.
- **Fix:** write `/revoked-at-cut/` only after the publish confirms, next to `record_cut_epoch_floor` in `drive_cut` and in `LinkSweep::cut`, or right after `:747`. Keep the revocation floor itself before the publish. A missing key already never clears, so a failed or lost-ack cut stays restrictive. Add a test: record the floor, fail the publish, then run a second cut from the N-1 base. R' must stay withheld.

**2. should-fix: one claim can stop the sweep from ever cutting an expired write link.** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a9ff3b5e78b5c6b87/crates/engine/src/facade/claim_conversion.rs:354`, together with `crates/engine/src/grants/cut_set.rs` `expired_links` and `facade/link_sweep.rs:134`. - **Scenario:** anyone holding a leaked Write link posts a claim just before the deadline. The tick acks it, and `convert_at` fails at the write-scope cut, so the entry stays pending. `acked_at` is before the deadline, so the claim stays convertible. The sweep excludes the link on every pass. The holder keeps reading through the link blob past the deadline until the owner opens the share dialog, runs "convert claims", or revokes by hand. ADR 0025 E1 bounds this window at "until the owner's sweep runs"; here the sweep runs and skips the link.
- **Fix:** before the sweep cuts a folder with due links, have it run a conversion whose `cut_write_scope` drives an `OwnerCutNet`. `LinkSweep` already holds `owner_pointer_seed` and builds one. Alternatively, emit an owner event for "expired link held by a stuck conversion".

The owner also grants H directly from an imported contact K1. `create_grant` has no identity de-dup; only conversion de-dups by identity (`invite.rs:985`). Revoking H removes one row and H keeps the other.

**4. nit: a hostile index entry can hide any deeper scope from the sweep, not only nested ones.** `/Users/myankelev/Code/random/cipher-box/.claude/worktrees/agent-a9ff3b5e78b5c6b87/crates/engine/src/facade/link_sweep.rs:180`. Confidence 5.

The walk reaches the bogus entry first, the resolve fails, and Q is marked visited. The real path to Q is skipped, so Q's whole subtree is never swept.

   - Dedup by `scope_id` ends cycles.

Three of your sub-reviews reported to the orchestrator, not to you. Do not wait on them. Fold these in with the crypto-privacy and simplify results you hold and return ONE final consolidated report.

SECURITY (2 should-fix, 3 nits): (1) `cascade.rs:730/557`: `/revoked-at-cut/` is written in `record_revocation_floor` BEFORE `publish_scope_root` at `:747`; when the publish fails (crash, lost ack, lost race) the device stays at cut epoch N-1, a later cut from that base signs N again, and `N >= cut_at(N)` clears the cut of a recipient whose cut never landed; fix: write `/revoked-at-cut/` only after the publish confirms, next to `record_cut_epoch_floor` in `drive_cut` and `LinkSweep::cut`; test: record, fail publish, second cut from N-1, the recipient stays withheld. (2) `claim_conversion.rs:354` + `cut_set.rs expired_links` + `link_sweep.rs:134`: a Write-permission claim at a scope still at `MINT_EPOCH` stays pending on every tick (`TickSites::cut_write_scope` returns Seam), so `expired_links` skips that link for ever and a leaked write link reads past its deadline until the dialog opens; fix: the sweep runs a conversion whose `cut_write_scope` drives an `OwnerCutNet` (the sweep holds `owner_pointer_seed`), or emits an owner event. NOTE: PR 1988's fold gives the tick the cut authority; judge whether that closes it after the rebase. (3) nit `cut_set.rs:28`: `committed_person` uses `.find`, one row per identity; two attested rows for one identity under different tags leave the second standing; collect every matching row, refuse Downgrade on more than one. (4) nit `link_sweep.rs:180`: `visited` is marked before the resolve, so a hostile index entry pointing at a deeper scope hides that subtree from the sweep (wider than ADR 0025 E3); mark visited only after a successful gated resolve. (5) nit `link_sweep.rs:141,206` + `facade.rs:7467`: `report.failure.get_or_insert` keeps the first error, so an early Seam hides a later TrustViolation from the abuse event; give TrustViolation priority. Clean: recipient key only from owner-attested rows, `via_link` inside the signed binding, fail-closed refusals, D3 clear keys cannot collide and `/cleared/` lowers no floor, `Running::hold` is RAII with no await between conversion and hold, sweep bounded by `MAX_DIRECT_CHILD_SCOPES`, no clock/RNG, no logging, codec refuses a non-boolean flag.

SPEC (2 should-fix, nits): (1) "Device B stops withholding P after device A commits P again" has only cascade unit tests that seed B's floors by hand; add an `owner_actions` test: phone revokes P, owner converts P again through a new link, phone rotates, P's blob is present. (2) `facade.rs:8362-8368`: every person revoke holds the conversion lock and fails at `:9223` when it is busy, also for a person no link admitted, while the 10-minute sweep holds the lock for its whole walk; refuse only when `person_cut_set` returns `admitting_link: Some`, take the lock after the resolve. (3) nit `cascade.rs:546-563`: a cut floor recorded before this release has no `/revoked-at-cut/` entry and never clears (fails toward restriction; note as accepted). (4) nit `owner_actions.rs:~5305`: assert the claimant still holds a grant after the Downgrade and before `revoke_link(true)`. All acceptance items confirmed otherwise; the walk's "one resolve and one unseal per scope root" is confirmed by code only, no test counts resolves.

STANDARDS: hard: the ADR 0023 D4 rationale ("the cut removes the link row the conversion reads, so the cut and the pass exclude each other") is restated at `claim_conversion.rs:121-123`, `facade.rs:9212-9215`, `:7424-7425`, `:8349-8351`, `link_sweep.rs:7-10`, `cut_set.rs:105-107`; home is the `Running` doc, the rest becomes a bare cross-reference. Judgement: absence-justifying lines `facade.rs:8346` "no contact book is read", `cut_set.rs:6` "never by the device-local contact book"; "checkbox" is a UI word in `owner_actions.rs:5182,5210,5213,5283` and `cut_set.rs:300` (the field is `remove_grantees`); `profile.rs:185` test message says "the 30 s tick" but the CI tick is 1 s; `owner_actions.rs:5231` asserts a fixture. Smells: `OwnerCutNet {..}` literal in `link_sweep.rs:246-271` repeats `facade.rs:8511-8536` and drops the write-report bookkeeping with `vault_pointer_signer: None`, safe only because a link entry is always `read`; nothing asserts that: refuse release-active when `report.write.is_some()` or share the net-plus-floor step; `net()` in `link_sweep.rs:64-90` duplicates `claim_conversion.rs:167-191`; pending-senders load duplicated (`facade.rs:9226-9235`, `link_sweep.rs:121-133`); the attested-and-Personal predicate twice in `cut_set.rs:29-35, :93-97`; the cadence check at `facade.rs:7427-7428` repeats `:6641-6642` without the backward-clock rationale; `LinkSweep` (18 fields) carries the same seam bundle as `ConversionPass`; signer/keys/factory cloned every tick before the `sweep_due` check (`facade.rs:7429-7431`); `PersonCut`/`committed_person` should be `GranteeCut` per CONTEXT.md. Gates: all Rust tests in "Engine simulation tests", the client test in "Shared packages typecheck + tests".

<result>All three review findings are fixed in one commit and one push. The new head of PR 1986 is `7faab9701`. CI is green: all 45 checks pass, none failed or pending. I requested no review. The first wait script ran past its limit and went to the background, so I started a second one; both have finished.

1. **Greptile `facade.rs:8668`, published link lacks owner setup:** fixed.
   - The mint now returns an `InviteMintOutcome { link, read_scope, stalled }` instead of a tuple. The owner's session registers the scope and keeps its read seed before the fragment comes back, on every path.
   - Your suggested fix alone was not enough. With only registration and the seed, the owner's next write into the folder was still sealed under the parent scope, and the link holder could not see it. A test showed this.
   - So a stalled mint now also starts a sweep of the parent scope, using the existing sweep factory. The sweep's index repair adds the new scope root to the parent, so the parent update is the only deferred work.
   - A stalled move of the folder's inner items is still finished only by a later mint of the same folder.
   - Test `a_stalled_link_mint_leaves_the_owner_reading_the_folder`: after a parent publish failure, with no second mint, an owner write into the folder reaches the link holder. It fails without the sweep.
2. **CodeRabbit `facade.rs:9256-9260`, `GrantSetFull` blocks later claims:** fixed as you specified. The failure is recorded, the item is not acked, and the pass continues. There is no test, because filling the set needs 1024 committed rows.
3. **CodeRabbit outside-diff `facade.rs:9273`, expired-link claims are never acked:** fixed. `LinkExpired` moved to the ack arm, and `LinkNotCommitted` and `ScopeMismatch` stay in the `continue` arm. Test `a_claim_on_an_expired_link_is_acked_and_stops_counting`: the claim is acked, grants nothing and no longer counts as waiting.

- **Threads:** I replied in both threads and resolved them through GraphQL. Each posted reply was read back and matches the text sent.
- **Disposition comment:** it lists all three items, including the outside-diff one, with the PR 1988 note: https://github.com/FSM1/cipher-box/pull/1986#issuecomment-5827401326
- **Local checks:** fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, the wasm32 check and the workspace tests pass. Both `kat_gen` runs show no drift, and `lint:tracker-refs` passes. The attribution grep prints nothing.

**Test helpers:** the helper `settle_filed_sweeps` now drives the sweep that a stalled mint starts. Any test that stalls a mint must call it before `recipient_session`. Otherwise the session picks up the finished sweep task and polls it again, which panics.

**Public items for lanes E and F:**
- New `InviteMintOutcome`, exported from `grants`.
- `mint_invite_link` now returns `InviteMintOutcome`.
- The crate-internal `promote_grantee_scope` now returns `PromotedGrant { read_scope, handover }`.</result>

Issue: FSM1/cipher-box#1975. Read it with `env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh issue view 1975`. Read ~/.claude/scratch/w1963/common.md first. Read the PR 1986 body and `crates/engine/src/grants/link_read.rs` and the `claim_invite_link` command in `facade.rs` first. Lanes E (PR 1988, claim + conversion) and F (PR 1987, append + permission change) rebase onto main now and touch `facade.rs` claim and grant commands; keep your facade edits inside a new preview command to limit conflicts.

Branch: `feat/1975-engine-link-preview`. Scratchpad: `~/.claude/scratch/w1963/H/` only.
PR title: `feat(engine): preview a link before join with nothing persisted and nothing posted`.

## Work
1. Recon: `crates/engine/src/grants/link_read.rs`, `net/pointer_fetch.rs`, `grants/received_status.rs` (the link-held read and the one-level listing source), `facade.rs` (`claim_invite_link`, the read-only snapshot paths), the seam stores (floors, snapshot cache, staging), `crates/wasm/src/lib.rs`, `packages/client` facade and worker protocol, `crates/engine/tests/owner_actions.rs`.
2. Add a preview command that runs the link read path with NOTHING persisted and nothing posted: no floor write, no snapshot cache write, no cut-epoch raise, no sequence raise, no bookmark, no claim post, no contact-book record. Use a no-persist wrapper over the seams (a read-through view that refuses writes) rather than flags inside the read path. The preview verifies the re-point object and the owner-signed names; a `Rejected` consult is a TrustViolation; an unavailable pointer or root answers an "unresolvable" preview state.
3. Return: the folder name and the owner name only when the fragment signature verifies (a bad signature returns no names and the link still works); the permission that conversion will grant (`conversion_permission` of the link entry); the link state (live, expired, revoked, unresolvable); a one-level listing of names and kinds from one read of the root (no sizes, no counts, no browse). Join stays the separate existing command.
4. Expose the preview through `crates/wasm` and the `packages/client` facade and worker protocol (a typed result; string literals, no enums).
5. Tests in the Rust gate (Engine simulation tests): the preview leaves every seam store byte-identical (snapshot the fake stores before and after); a forged name yields no names; the listing has names and kinds only; a forged re-point is a TrustViolation with no store change; an expired link previews as expired. Client codec test for the result shape.
6. Run `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine`, `cargo test --workspace --exclude fuser --exclude cipherbox-desktop`, `cargo fmt --all --check`, clippy `-D warnings`, the wasm32 check, `pnpm install`, `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, the client unit tests, `pnpm lint:tracker-refs`.
7. Open the DRAFT PR with `--base main`. Body ends with `Closes #1975.` Wait for CI green with one polling script. Report.
EOF

S1. `rotation/cascade.rs:730` and `:557`: `/revoked-at-cut/` is written in `record_revocation_floor` BEFORE `publish_scope_root` (`:747`). When the publish fails (crash, lost ack, lost race) the device stays at cut epoch N-1, a later cut from that base signs N again, and `N >= cut_at(N)` clears the cut of a recipient whose cut never landed. Fix: write `/revoked-at-cut/` only after the publish confirms, next to `record_cut_epoch_floor` in `drive_cut` and in `LinkSweep::cut`. Keep the revocation floor before the publish. Test: record the floor, fail the publish, run a second cut from the N-1 base, the recipient stays withheld.
S2. `facade/claim_conversion.rs:354` + `cut_set.rs expired_links` + `link_sweep.rs:134`: a Write claim at a scope still at `MINT_EPOCH` stayed pending on every tick, so `expired_links` skipped that link for ever and a leaked write link read past its deadline. After the rebase the tick holds the cut authority (PR 1988 fold). Verify on the rebased branch that the sweep's conversion pass runs the write-scope cut; if a path still leaves such a claim pending, close it. Test: an expired write link with a pending write claim at a read-only folder is converted and cut by the next sweep on the other owner device.
S3. `facade.rs:8362-8368`: every person revoke holds the conversion lock and fails at `:9223` when it is busy, also for a person no link admitted, while the 10-minute sweep holds the lock for its whole walk. Fix: take the lock after the resolve and refuse only when `person_cut_set` returns `admitting_link: Some`. Test: a direct grantee's revoke succeeds while the sweep runs.
S4. Test gap: "device B stops withholding P after device A commits P again" has only cascade unit tests that seed B's floors by hand. Add an `owner_actions` test: the phone revokes P, the owner converts P again through a new link (or appends P; use what the rebased base offers), the phone rotates, P's blob is present.
S5. `cut_set.rs:28`: `committed_person` uses `.find`, one row per identity; two attested rows for one identity under different tags leave the second standing. Collect every matching row into the cut set; `Downgrade`/`ChangePermission` refuses when more than one row matches.
S6. `link_sweep.rs:180`: `visited` is marked before the resolve, so a hostile index entry that points at a deeper scope hides that subtree from the sweep (wider than ADR 0025 E3). Mark visited only after a successful gated resolve and let a later parent take over a child whose resolve failed.
S7. `link_sweep.rs:141,206` + `facade.rs:7467`: `report.failure.get_or_insert` keeps the first error, so an early Seam hides a later TrustViolation from the abuse event. Give TrustViolation priority.
S8. `link_sweep.rs:246-271`: the `OwnerCutNet {..}` literal repeats `facade.rs:8511-8536`, drops the write-report bookkeeping and hard-codes `vault_pointer_signer: None`; this is safe only because a link entry is always `read`, and nothing asserts it. Share the net-plus-floor step with `drive_cut`, and refuse release-active when `report.write.is_some()` on the sweep path.

N1. The ADR 0023 D4 rationale ("the cut removes the link row the conversion reads, so the cut and the pass exclude each other") is restated at `claim_conversion.rs:121-123`, `facade.rs:9212-9215`, `:7424-7425`, `:8349-8351`, `link_sweep.rs:7-10`, `cut_set.rs:105-107`. "checkbox" is a UI word (`owner_actions.rs:5182,5210,5213,5283`, `cut_set.rs:300`): use `remove_grantees`. `PersonCut`/`committed_person` → `GranteeCut`/`committed_grantee` (CONTEXT.md term). `profile.rs:185` test message "the 30 s tick" is wrong for the CI profile (1 s): make the message profile-neutral. `owner_actions.rs:5231` asserts a fixture only: delete. `owner_actions.rs:~5305`: assert the claimant still holds a grant after the Downgrade and before `revoke_link(true)`.

Fix: on the same-permission retry path re-record the grant floor (an idempotent raise) before the pointer post. Test: fail the floor write on the first grant, retry, the floor is raised.
3. `facade.rs:11126` "Name cache blocks sharing reads": a corrupt device-local name cache makes `names()` return an error and `?` fails the whole `sharing()` read. Do not request a CodeRabbit review. Prose in Simplified Technical English. No attribution.

1. `facade/claim_conversion.rs:539` "Failed delivery loses its retry": when the grant is published but the share-pointer post fails, the pass marks the claim settled and removes its conversion entry, so a claimant converted near the deadline holds a grant with no pointer. Fix: keep the entry in a "granted, pointer pending" state and retry the pointer post on later passes until it lands; settle only after the post succeeds. Test: fail the post once, the next pass posts the pointer and settles.
2. `claim_conversion.rs:362` "Ack can erase the claim": when the ack removes the item but the conversion record save fails, the claim has no durable copy. Fix: persist the claim into the record in an "acking" state BEFORE the DELETE, run the DELETE, then mark it acked and persist. On a retry an entry still in "acking" converts regardless of the DELETE answer, because a second conversion of a known identity is a no-op (the ADR 0023 D5 lock stays: a fresh claim still needs `removed: true` before it enters the record). Test: crash between the ack and the record save, a fresh engine on the same store converts the claim.
3. `claim_conversion.rs:635` "Failed re-point strands moved child": the write-scope move completes before the parent's child index publish; when the parent publish fails, the stored index names the old root and later walks cannot find the moved child. Fix: on a parent publish failure after a move, file the parent sweep that main already uses for a stalled link mint (the sweep's index repair adds the moved root), so the walk finds the child on the next pass. Test: fail the parent publish after the move, the next sweep repairs the index and the pending conversion completes.
4. `facade.rs:9207` "Revoke ignores failed conversion": when the preliminary conversion pass cannot poll the mailbox, the revoke continues with the link cut and an unacked inbox claim is stranded. Fix: a failed poll refuses the revoke with a retryable `Seam` error ("mailbox unavailable"); the owner retries. Test: a mailbox outage refuses the link revoke and the link stays committed.

Run the engine tests, the workspace tests, fmt, clippy, the wasm32 check, both `kat_gen` runs, and the client tests if a facade type changed. Report the new head SHA and any changed public item.
