<result># Review of PR 1993 (feat/1977-web-share-dialog, head ddb243413)

Evidence: `pnpm typecheck` passes; `pnpm --filter @cipherbox/web test` passes (68 files, 789 tests); every PR check is green at ddb243413. No git write, no browser, no nested agent.

## Findings

### should-fix

1. `apps/web/src/hooks/useSharingActions.ts:168-175` — `revokeInviteLink(linkTag, _options)` drops `removeGrantees` in silence. CONFIRMED.
   Scenario: PR 1988 (conversion writes `via_link`) merges before PR 1989 (client option). The checkbox shows, the owner ticks "also remove the 1 person", confirms, the link is cut, the person keeps access, no error shows. Today the checkbox never shows on main (grep finds no production write of `via_link`), so the window opens at the 1988 merge.
   Fix (fail closed, one line; the fold replaces it):
   ```ts
   run('revokeInviteLink', async (facade) => {
     if (options.removeGrantees) throw new Error('removing the people who joined is not in this build');
     await facade.revokeInviteLink(target, linkTag);
   ```
   Add one vitest: the checked confirm reports that refusal and keeps the link.

2. `apps/web/src/components/sharing/LinkSection.tsx:97-105` — the mint stays enabled while `fresh` shows, so a second mint replaces the shown-once link. CONFIRMED.
   Scenario: the owner mints a read link, does not copy it, changes to write, mints again. The first link is live, holds a grant-set slot and an admission cap, and no one can ever hold it. The `minting` ref guards only the double click.
   Fix: `disabled={busy || fresh !== null}` on `share-mint-link`, or hold `fresh` as a list and render one `CopyableValue` per mint.

### nit

3. `LinkSection.tsx:49-50` — `storeOwnerName(name)` runs before the mint. A name the engine refuses (`invite-name-too-long`) persists and pre-fills every later open. Move the store into `.then` when `fragment !== null`.
4. `apps/web/src/sharing/ownerName.ts:5-8`, `EngineProvider.tsx:73` — `forgetOwnerName` runs only in the effect cleanup. A tab close skips it, so the next account on the browser sees the previous owner's label. A label, not a key. Either accept and drop the "later account does not inherit it" claim, or key the entry by a session value.
5. `ShareDialog.tsx:81` — "people with access · 1" renders beside "people unavailable" when `scope === null`. Hide the count when `scope` is null.
6. `useSharingActions.ts:170` — the comment states a condition ("takes no `removeGrantees` yet"); drop "yet" so it stays true until the fold changes it.
7. `PeopleTable.tsx:119-160` and `LinkSection.tsx:211-278` — two confirmations with one shape (title, notes, keep, danger button, `role="alertdialog"`). A small `Confirm` primitive would hold both. Not required for merge.
8. Props `busy` and `actions` both travel; `busy` is `actions.busy !== null` (`ShareDialog.tsx:44`). Derive it in the children, or keep as is.
9. Rename has vitest coverage only; no Playwright step edits a name. Acceptable with the "Human verification" list in the PR body.

## Answers to the implementer's gaps

1. Admission cap. Engine: `Command::CreateInviteLink` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:1255`) gets `admission_cap: Option<u64>`; `create_invite_link` (`facade.rs:8802`) maps `None` to `DEFAULT_ADMISSION_CAP` and refuses `0` or a value above a new `pub const MAX_ADMISSION_CAP: u64` (beside `DEFAULT_ADMISSION_CAP` at `crates/engine/src/grants/invite.rs:283`; bound it under the grant-set capacity that fires `grant-set-full`) with `MalformedInput { check: "invite-admission-cap-out-of-range" }`, then `LinkTerms { admission_cap }`. Wasm: `create_invite_link(node, permission, expires_at, owner_name, admission_cap: Option<u64>)` (`crates/wasm/src/lib.rs:2044`). Client: `protocol.ts:585` descriptor gets `admissionCap: number | null`; `commandCodec.ts:367` passes it through a bounded-integer check; `facade.ts:392` gets `admissionCap?: number`. Web: `LinkSection` adds `<input type="number" min={1} max={MAX}>` with default 25; the hook gets a fourth argument; `shareRefusals.ts` gets a label for the new check. Tests: an engine unit test for the refusal (release-active `Err`), a codec test, a vitest for the input.
2. Conversion on open. Harmless now: `convert_invite_claims` (`facade.rs:9674-9684`) polls the mailbox first and returns `Ok` on an empty inbox; the cost is one mailbox poll per open of a folder with a link. Removal after 1988: delete the second `run('convertInviteClaims', ...)` block in `useSharingActions.open` (`useSharingActions.ts:104-113`) and return `reached`; drop `'convertInviteClaims'` from `SharingCommand` and the vitest cases that assert the call. Note that ADR 0023 D4 itself names "when the owner opens the share dialog" as a trigger, so the web call goes only if 1988 puts that trigger inside the engine (for example in the sharing read).
3. No grant time exists. `GrantLedgerEntry` (`crates/core/src/seal/write_body.rs:76-`) carries tag, recipient keys, permission, `owner_sig`, `via_link`, `grantee_name`; the commitment entry carries `deadline` only on a link entry; ADR 0023 D2 retired the row `expiresAt`. A signed `grantedAt` is a wire-format change with an ADR. The column is correctly dropped.
4. "X joined": correct to fold after 1988. `granteeJoined` is absent from `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts` on main.
5. `via_link` on the read. Sourced only from an owner-attested row: `project_grant_ledger` (`facade.rs:4369`) filters by `row_is_owner_attested`, and `via_link` is inside the signed preimage (`insert_optional_signed`, `write_body.rs:274-277`, used by `encode_recipient_binding`). The test `a_via_link_tag_reaches_the_host_only_on_an_owner_attested_row` lives in `facade.rs` `mod tests`, which runs in "Rust / Engine simulation tests" (`ci-rust.yml:78`) and "Workspace tests". It proves an unsigned row drops the tag; a tampered `via_link` on a signed row is covered in core (`write_body.rs:1260`).
6. `localStorage` holds one key, `cipherbox.share.ownerName` (`ownerName.ts`); the other users (`sealedStore.ts`, `coreKit.ts`, `wagmi.ts`) are pre-existing. `EngineProvider` clears it in the effect cleanup (sign-out and rebuild). Gap: nit 4.
7. The failing spec is stale on main, not changed by this PR. Since PR 1986 a claim records a link hold (`facade.rs:9645 received.hold_link`) and `received_shares` lists every hold as a row with `via_link: true` (`facade.rs:11108-11119`), so the claimant's `/shared` page shows one row and `shared-empty` never appears. In that spec the owner's dialog closes before the claim (`tests/web-e2e/sharing.ts:mint`), so this PR runs no conversion there. Conversion on open is lawful under ADR 0023 D4. The full Web E2E workflow last ran 2026-09-19, before 1986 merged, so no main run shows the break. Fix in this PR: assert `shared-list` has one row that reads as a link hold with no grant, in place of `empty`.

## Gate verdicts

- /simplify: nothing blocking. Nits 5-8.
- /security-review: refusal labels fail closed (`Object.hasOwn`, verbatim fallback, `constructor` and `__proto__` tested). The fragment shows only through `CopyableValue`, lives in the dialog's React state until unmount, never in the store, a URL query, or a log (no `console.` in the sharing tree). Names, fingerprints and check ids render as React text or attributes; no `dangerouslySetInnerHTML`. One fail-open: finding 1.
- /crypto-privacy-review: clean. The web builds no fragment; the owner name goes to the engine, which signs it into the fragment; the fingerprint comes from `facade.identityFingerprint`. No crypto in TypeScript.
- /code-review: every acceptance line maps to a test in "Web host typecheck + tests" (create link, revoke link with and without the checkbox, change permission, rename, no "convert claims" control) and "Web E2E" (mint, revoke, downgrade, conversion on open). No `.spec.ts` under vitest. Page objects updated. PR body: no attribution, bare `Closes #1977.`, title has no parentheses beyond the scope. Gap: item 7 in the e2e suite.

Note: the harness refused a findings file write under `~/.claude/scratch`, so this message is the only copy of the report.</result>

cat > /tmp/issue-origin.md <<'EOF'
## Problem

The owner's contact book records, for each contact a link admitted, the blinded tag of that link (`LinkOrigin.link_tag` in `crates/engine/src/grants/contact_store.rs`). A blinded tag is bound to the scope root name, and a write-scope cut moves the root, so every link tag at that folder changes at each write wave (the entries are rebound with `GrantSetEntry::rebound`). The contact book keeps the old tag. After one write wave at a folder:

- `link_budget_full` charges the per-link contact share against the new tag, finds no contact sourced by it, and the share of that link resets to empty. The cap on contacts one link can admit stops working for any link minted before the wave.
- The sharing read reports `contactBudgetFull: false` for a link that filled its share before the wave.
- A link revoke with `remove_grantees` (added in the revoke slice) finds the people the link admitted through the same origin; after a wave it finds nobody for a row whose owner signature a writer broke, so that row survives the revoke. The owner can still revoke that person directly.

## Fix

Record the link by a value that does not move. The link's ephemeral identity key (`CommittedLink::ephemeral_identity_pk`) is stable across waves; key the origin by it, or rebind the origins in the contact book at the cut, where the engine holds the old-to-new tag map. Keep the encoded contact record readable by the current release on staging: write the new field beside `linkTag` and read either, or rebind in place. One engine simulation test: a link admits a contact, a write claim converts through the write-scope cut, the link's share still counts that contact and a link revoke with the flag still reaches a row whose signature a writer broke.

## Acceptance

- [ ] The per-link contact share survives a write wave.
- [ ] `contactBudgetFull` on the sharing read survives a write wave.
- [ ] A link revoke with `remove_grantees` reaches a broken row after a write wave.
- [ ] Tests in the "Engine simulation tests" gate.

Part of #1963.
EOF

# usage: slot-pick.sh <HHMM-utc-start> <pr:oldhead> [<pr:oldhead> ...]

START=$1; shift
while [ "$(date -u +%H%M)" -lt "$START" ]; do sleep 60; done
for try in $(seq 1 30); do
  for spec in "$@"; do
    pr=${spec%%:*}; old=${spec##*:}
    head=$(env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr view $pr --json headRefOid,isDraft,state --jq 'select(.isDraft==false and .state=="OPEN") | .headRefOid[0:9]')

    [ "$red" != "0" ] && continue
    echo "$(date -u +%H:%M) requesting CodeRabbit on PR $pr head $head"
    env -u GITHUB_TOKEN gh pr comment $pr --body "@coderabbitai review" >/dev/null

done

## Problem

`stagedBytes` in `packages/client/src/seams/stagingStore.ts` opens an exclusive OPFS sync access handle for every read. When two engine paths read the same staged file at the same time, the second read fails with `Access Handles cannot be created if there is another open Access Handle`.

Serialize access to one file: queue reads and writes of the same path behind one promise chain in the staging store (per-path mutex), so a second reader waits for the handle to close. - [ ] A read during a write of the same file resolves after the write.
- [ ] Test in the "Shared packages typecheck + tests" gate.

## Problem

A contact's encryption subkey can change in the owner's contact book while an older committed row still carries the old key, and the person revoke then misses that row. Two paths in `crates/engine/src/grants/contact_store.rs`: `record_from_link` removes the held entry and pushes the new contact with no subkey compare (only `record_unchanged_from_link` refuses `RecipientKeyChanged`), and the hand import `record` replaces the entry unconditionally.

Scenario: write grantee W (identity I, key K1) strips its own row R1 so it is unattested. W re-claims through an open link with code (I, K2): the blinded tag is over the shared secret, so the tag is new, the held-grant lookup by identity matches attested rows only, and the claim is granted as a new row R2 with the book now I to K2. The owner revokes I: `revoked_rows` takes R2 by identity, but R1 is unattested and K1 differs from K2, so R1 survives and the rotation re-seals its blob for K1. W keeps reading. `record_from_link` refuses `claim-recipient-key-changed` when the held entry's subkey differs, as the unchanged path does. <result>CodeRabbit's finding is **real**. I fixed it, rebased the branch on the new main, and pushed once. The thread has my reply and is resolved.

**Why it is real (PR 1993, comment 4109721701)**

The engine can cut people that the dialog does not show:
- `project_grant_ledger` in `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` (about line 4654) sends `viaLink` and the name only on a row that the owner attests. On any other row, `viaLink` is `null`.
- `link_cut_set` in `crates/engine/src/grants/cut_set.rs` (about lines 186-215) takes a row in two cases:
  - Its `via_link` equals the link tag, even when the writer broke the owner signature. The projection hides that tag.
  - The row has no attested label, and a contact that the link sourced holds its key. The `LinkSource` can be `Identity` or the legacy `Tag`.
- After a link is re-keyed, `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:4296-4339` moves the `via_link` of attested rows to the new tag, so those rows agree. An unattested row gets the placeholder label and no `via_link`. Its projected `viaLink` is `null`, but the cut still takes it through the contact book.
- The legacy `LinkSource::Tag` window never makes the cut bigger than what the dialog shows. After a write wave, the old tag stops matching and the cut gets smaller.

Before the fix, the dialog hid the choice when no visible row named the link and always sent `false`. Those people kept access.

**The fix (commit ef79045c7, `fix(web): always offer the remove choice on a link revoke`)**
- `apps/web/src/components/sharing/LinkSection.tsx`: the revoke prompt always shows the remove checkbox and sends the owner's choice to the engine unchanged. It still lists the people whose row names the link. It shows a count ("1 person") only when that list is exact.
- `apps/web/src/sharing/inviteLink.ts`: new `unclearGrants` returns the rows with no name and no link. A row with a name is attested, so the engine cuts it only when its visible `viaLink` matches. Only a row with no name and no link can hide a joiner. The prompt shows `// N grant(s) with no name and no link may have joined through it` only when such a row exists. Where the list is exact, it shows no hedge.
- `apps/web/src/stores/sharing.store.ts` and `packages/client/src/worker/protocol.ts`: the `viaLink` doc now says that `null` also means a row the owner does not attest.
- Tests in `ShareDialog.test.tsx` and `inviteLink.test.ts`:
  - Updated three existing tests.
  - Added two dialog tests: the unclear note appears and `true` is sent, and `true` is sent when no row names the link.
  - Added one `unclearGrants` unit test.
- The e2e page object needed no change, because `revokeFirstLink` does not use the checkbox.

**Rebase onto 53191d913 (PR 1994)**
- `tests/web-e2e/page-objects/share.page.ts`: I kept this branch's version. Main's `liveLinkExpiry` and `revokeLinkButton` belong to the old live-link panel. This branch replaced that panel with chips and no spec uses them now. The branch's `openUntilGranted` default is 180 s with a 30 s inner wait, so main's calls that pass a timeout still work.
- `tests/cross-client/src/share.ts`: I kept the branch's `toHaveValue('read')`, because the permission is now a select. Main's `grantee.openFiles()` merged in without a conflict.
- `tests/web-e2e/staging/invite.spec.ts`: I kept main's join flow and used the branch's `toHaveValue('read')`.

### 2022
engine: an owner device reads no sharing state after another owner device's write-scope cut
bug,v2-build,comp:engine
Device A of an owner cannot read the sharing state of a folder after device B of the same owner did a write-scope cut on that folder.

## How to see it

1. Device A makes a folder and mints a read link. A holder joins, and device B converts the claim. Device A reads the share dialog correctly at this point.
2. Device A mints a write link and goes offline. A second holder joins. Device B converts the claim. This conversion does a write-scope cut, which moves the folder scope root (ADR 0024 D4).
3. Device A signs in again and opens the share dialog of the folder.

## Result

- Device A shows "people unavailable — no read reached this folder". The link chips and the grant rows do not show. The engine `sharing` read gives `state: null`.
- The result stays the same for 3 minutes of repeated opens, and after a new sign-in on device A.
- Device B reads the same folder correctly: 2 link chips and 2 grant rows.
- A fresh third device on the same account reads the folder correctly.
- Device A still reads the folder contents. Only the sharing read fails.

So device-local state that device A kept from before the cut stops the owner sharing read (`scope_sharing` in `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` returns `None`). Device A cannot revoke the write link, and it cannot mint or grant on that folder.

## Expected

Device A reads the moved scope root and shows the same links and grants as device B.

## Test

`tests/web-e2e/tests/link-first.spec.ts`, test "device A revokes the write link with its joiners: the writer fails closed and the reader keeps access". The test is marked `test.fail` with this condition. It runs in the Web E2E Full slice. The fix must remove the `test.fail` call, and the test must pass. The fix can then add the same step to `tests/web-e2e/staging/link-first.spec.ts`.

### 2023
engine: a write link holder keeps a read view in its session after conversion
bug,v2-build,comp:engine
A holder that joined through a write link keeps a read-only view of the folder in the same session after the owner converts the claim.

## How to see it

1. The owner mints a write link. A holder joins through it. The page opens the shared folder read-only, as expected before conversion.
2. An owner device converts the claim.
3. In the same holder session, `/shared` shows the row as `granted`, permission `write`, `data-via-link="false"`.
4. The holder opens the folder from `/shared` and does a manual refresh every 2 seconds for 2 minutes.

## Result

The file browser keeps the notice "this folder was shared with you. you can open and download what is in it." It shows no "new folder" button and no upload zone. The engine snapshot of the folder gives `permission: 'read'`.

After a new sign-in (a new session), the same holder gets `permission: 'write'` at once and can write.

A local full run of the Web E2E suite with 2 workers also showed this symptom once in `tests/web-e2e/tests/write-grant.spec.ts` (a direct write grant by contact code). That spec passed when it ran alone. So the same cause can make that smoke spec flaky.

## Expected

The session that holds the folder gets write when the conversion lands, with no new sign-in (ADR 0023: each URL holder becomes a writer after conversion, with no owner step).

## Test

`tests/web-e2e/tests/link-first.spec.ts`, test "a write link holder writes after device B converts, and device A reads the write", and step 4 in `tests/web-e2e/staging/link-first.spec.ts`. Both sign the writer in again after the conversion. The fix must remove that second sign-in, and both tests must pass.

### 2024
web: a person the owner cut cannot join again through a new link
bug,v2-build,comp:web
A person that the owner cut cannot join the folder again through a new link.

## How to see it

1. The owner mints a read link. A holder joins, and an owner device converts the claim.
2. An owner device revokes the holder (a person revoke). The `/shared` row of the holder goes to `revocation-signal`.
3. The owner mints a new read link on the same folder. The holder opens it and signs in.

## Result

The invite page goes to state `joined` and shows only "open folder". It shows no "join". So the holder cannot send a claim, and no owner device can convert it again.

## Expected

The invite page lets a person that the owner cut join again through a new link. ADR 0025 D3 names this case: one owner device cuts a person, and the other owner device converts that person again.

## Test

`tests/web-e2e/tests/link-first.spec.ts`, test "a reader that device B cut and device A admitted again survives the next re-key on B", and step 6 in `tests/web-e2e/staging/link-first.spec.ts`. Both admit the reader again by a direct grant with contact codes. The fix must change that step to a join through a new link, and both tests must pass.

# Diagnosis #2022: owner device A reads no sharing state after device B's write-scope cut

## 1. Root cause (layer: engine)

I reproduced the defect in the engine simulation. The web and client layers behave correctly.

- **B's cut raises only B's floor.** The write-scope cut on device B runs a write wave. The wave moves the folder root and seals its owner-write-blob at write epoch 2. B raises only its own write-epoch floor (`crates/engine/src/facade/claim_conversion.rs:835`).
- **A keeps floor 1.** Device A kept write-epoch floor 1 for the folder scope from its own link mint. Floors are durable, so a new sign-in keeps them.
- **The seed does not open at floor 1.** The owner recovers the write scope seed only at the standing floor (`crates/engine/src/net/adopter.rs:640-653`, `open_write_scope_seed_at`). The blob at epoch 2 does not open at floor 1, so `write_scope_seed` is `None`. `write_plane_of_gated` then gives `ResolveFailure::Unavailable` (`crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:1602`).
- **The sharing read turns this into `null`.** `scope_sharing` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:11774`, `resolve_anchored(...).ok()?`) turns that failure into `state: None`.
- **All owner actions fail the same way.** Every owner action on the folder uses the same resolve (`OwnerRotationNet::gated_write_plane`, `rotation.rs:1805-1822`). In the simulation, a link mint on A after the cut also fails with `Seam("descendant record unavailable")`.
- **Nothing raises A's floor to 2.** Only a scope-pointer consult (`net/pointer_fetch.rs:134`) raises the floor of a device that did not run the wave. There are three consult paths, and none runs on A:
  - **Tick walk.** `ScopeWalk::recover_write_plane_from_pointer` (`rotation.rs:1401-1406`, from #1646) returns early "while a floor stands". A fresh device has no floor, so it consults and seeds floor 2. That is why the third device works.
  - **Polled tick consult.** It consults only `FocusWindow::open_shared_scopes` (`sync/tick.rs:166`). No production code fills that field, so no tick ever consults the owner's own interior scopes.
  - **On-access consult.** The owner access paths build their nets with `PointerConsultArm::Refused`. `ConsultReason::OnAccess` (`sync/pointer.rs:54`) is defined but has no caller.
- **Content reads still work** because the cut does not change the read plane.

## 2. Why the tests missed it

- `a_write_claim_converts_on_the_other_owner_devices_tick_with_one_cut` (`crates/engine/tests/owner_actions.rs:5480`) asserts the sharing read only on the converting device (the phone). The phone raised its own floor. The test never reads on the minting device.
- `a_claim_converts_on_the_owners_other_device` uses a read link, so no write wave runs.
- The #1646 tests cover a device with no floor. No test covers a device whose floor is below the pointer's write epoch after another owner device ran a write wave.

## 3. The fix

**Location.** The change goes in `crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs`, in `OwnerRotationNet::gated_write_plane`. All owner resolves go through this one function: the sharing read, mint, grant, revoke, conversion and repoint.

**Change.**
1. `write_plane_of_gated` gives `Unavailable` at `RootAnchor::Descendant`, and the section holds an owner-write-blob. In that case, run an on-access `PointerConsult::run` for the scope. It raises the write floor on sight.
2. Open the blob again at the new floor, set `root.write_scope_seed`, and read the write plane again.
3. If the pointer is absent or unavailable, give `Unavailable`. If the consult rejects the pointer, give `Rejected`.
4. `rotation.rs:2997` is a second `write_plane_of_gated` site. Check whether the sweep path needs the same change.

**Invariants to keep:**
- **A rejected pointer is a TrustViolation.** A rejected pointer (bad signature or write-epoch regression) must map to `ResolveFailure::Rejected` and then to `EngineError::TrustViolation` through `from_resolve_failure`, never to `Unavailable`. `scope_sharing` drops errors with `.ok()?`, so it must also emit a trust-violation event for a rejection.
- **Floors stay monotonic.** Only `PointerConsult` raises a floor, and only to the epoch the owner signed.
- **The stale-copy case does not change.** When the pointer epoch equals the floor, the blob still does not open and the answer stays `Unavailable`.
- **Other invariants.** No encode path changes, so encode/decode symmetry is not affected. The fix adds no clock, no RNG and no `debug_assert`.
- **`PointerConsultArm` doc.** The doc says a `Refused` pass consults nothing. Update it to name the on-access consult as a separate trigger, or pass a `ConsultReason::OnAccess` arm.

**Blueprint and glossary text the fix obeys:**
- `blueprint/engine.md` "Pointer planes": "the pointer resolve joins the focus-window tick for open shared scopes, runs on access for cached ones, and is the first act on cold start."
- `CONTEXT.md` "Scope pointer": "consulted on the sync tick for open shared scopes, on access for cached ones, and first on cold start."
- `CONTEXT.md` "Floor law": floors "cold-seed from the re-point object's owner-vouched epochs".

**Optional (same PR or a follow-up issue).** `ScopeWalk::recover_write_plane_from_pointer` can also consult when a floor stands and the blob does not open, paced by `pointer_consult_interval`. The tick would then repair A with no owner action. The e2e needs only the on-access fix.

**Prototype result.** The prototype makes the sharing read and the mint on A pass. The full `cargo test -p cipherbox-engine` suite passes with it (0 failures).

## 4. Regression test

Put it in `crates/engine/tests/owner_actions.rs`, next to line 5480, using `GrantScenario`:
1. Device A (`fx.engine`) mints a write link.
2. `post_claims` posts one claim.
3. A phone (`boot_owner` on a second `FakeDevice`) converts it on its tick.

<result>I found the engine root cause (#2023) and reproduced it in an engine test. I could not write `~/.claude/scratch/w1963/diag/2023/report.md` because the harness refused the write, so the full report is below. The temp worktree `/tmp/diag-2023` is removed. The repo has no changes, and the stash list is as it was. One open point: my test shows the holder's inability to write, but not the `permission: 'read'` flag that the e2e reports (section 1).

# #2023 diagnosis: a write link holder keeps a read view after conversion

## 1. Root cause (engine)

A session that joined through the link cannot write after the conversion. A new session on the same device writes at once.

- **The join:** the write link join adds the shared folder to the render tree at the old scope root name, R0. `merge_grafted` (`crates/engine/src/grants/received_status.rs:233`, the `None` arm near line 253) sets `meta.ipns_name` only when it creates the node.
- **The conversion:** it does a write-scope cut, which moves the scope root to R1 (`crates/engine/src/facade/claim_conversion.rs:618-647`, `cut_write_scope` at 810).
- **The bookmark moves to R1** by the pointer heal (`follow_held_pointers` / `HoldChange::Heal`) and by the `accept_share` reconcile (`grants/accept.rs:1231`). The personal blob opens at R1, and the write seed is deposited against R1. The `/shared` row shows `granted`, `write`, `via-link=false`.
- **The render node keeps R0.** The `Some(meta)` arm (`received_status.rs:248-251`) only renames. It never updates `ipns_name`.
- **The drain uses R0.** `grafted_write_passes` (`crates/engine/src/facade.rs:5035-5068`) takes its name from `base.node(root).ipns_name`, and the drain scope uses `root_name: &pass.name` (`facade.rs:7751-7760`). The R1 write seed does not derive R0. The drain treats this as the name-skew case, which waits with no event (`sync/drain.rs:7515`). So no write from that session ever lands.
- **A new session works** because it adds the folder from the bookmark, which is at R1.

**Evidence.** I added a test to `crates/engine/tests/owner_actions.rs` in the temp worktree. It runs: a read link and a reader, device B converts on its tick, a write link, the holder reads through the link, and B converts again.
- **Same session, before the fix:** the row changed to Write. A queued create stayed in the queue for every pass, with no dead letter and no hold.
- **New session:** it drained the create at once.
- **Same session, with the fix below:** it drained the create. All 1968 engine lib tests and all 190 `owner_actions` tests passed.
- The test and the fix are in `~/.claude/scratch/w1963/diag/2023/diag-repro-and-fix.patch`.

**Open point:** in my test, `SnapshotView.permission` changed to `Write` one tick after the row did. The e2e reports `read`, and I did not reproduce that. One likely cause:
- `grafted_write_roots` is set at `facade.rs:7602`, before the received-share pass at `facade.rs:7972` deposits the seed. So the permission changes one tick later, and no `SnapshotUpdated` event comes with that change.
- A host view painted between those ticks stays `read`. It changes only after another event or a pull, and the web pulls only when `manualRefresh` succeeds (`apps/web/src/engine/snapshotStore.ts`).
- This lag also fits the `write-grant.spec.ts` flake with 2 workers. A direct grant has no stale name, but it has this one-tick lag.

## 2. Why the existing tests missed it

- `received_status.rs` `a_root_a_write_wave_moved_still_opens_through_the_pointer` checks the healed bookmark and the listing. It does not check the render node's `ipns_name`.
- `owner_actions.rs` `a_write_link_mints_at_read_and_its_conversion_runs_one_write_cut` and `a_write_claim_converts_on_the_other_owner_devices_tick_with_one_cut` check only the owner side.
- The `WriteGrantee` harness (`facade.rs` tests, near line 19700) accepts a write grant directly, so its folder node already has the final name. No test adds the folder before the root moves and then writes.
- The name-skew wait sends no event, so nothing reports the failure.

## 3. The fix

1. **`merge_grafted` in `grants/received_status.rs`:** when the node exists and its `ipns_name` differs from `share.scope_root_name`, set it to the bookmark name. Include that change in the `SnapshotUpdated` condition. This is the patch I tested, about 10 lines.
2. **`facade.rs` near line 7602:** when the new `grafted_write_roots` set differs from the old one, send `Event::SnapshotUpdated`. Then the host repaints on the tick that proves or drops a write pass.

The fix must keep these invariants:
- The name comes only from the verified bookmark, healed by the owner-signed pointer (ADR 0024 D5 step 3) or by the gated `accept_share`. It never comes from a record's own word.
- `seed_names` / `deposit_write_seed` (`facade.rs:4801-4825`) stays the proof that the seed names the root.
- A gate rejection stays a TrustViolation.
- The fix adds no `debug_assert!`, no clock and no RNG. It changes no wire format or encode path, so encode/decode symmetry does not apply.

Normative text:
- **ADR 0024 D4:** "At conversion the owner engine mints the personal row at the conversion permission, with the write material and a write-scope cut when the folder has none yet … The grantee then writes under its own writer pseudonym."
- **ADR 0024 D2:** "The persist that records the first personal open also deletes `linkSecret`. The person is then a grantee."
- **ADR 0023**, as the issue states it: each URL holder becomes a writer after conversion, with no owner step.

## 4. Regression tests

- **Engine test in `crates/engine/tests/owner_actions.rs`.** It uses `GrantScenario`, `mint_link_at(Permission::Write)`, a holder session on `fx.recipient_device`, and a phone device at the owner identity that converts on its tick. The patch has the diagnostic version. The steps:
  1. The holder claims and ticks until the link read shows the folder.
  2. The phone ticks and converts.
  3. The holder ticks twice.
  4. Assert that `snapshot(shared).permission == Write`.
  5. Send `Command::Create` under the shared root and tick.
  6. Assert that the queue is empty and that the owner lists the child at the moved root.
- **Unit assertion in `a_root_a_write_wave_moved_still_opens_through_the_pointer`:** the render node of `SCOPE` has `ipns_name == scope_root_name()`.
- **For fix 2:** assert that `SnapshotUpdated` is sent on the tick where the root enters `grafted_write_roots`.
- **E2E:** step 4 of `tests/web-e2e/tests/link-first.spec.ts` and of `staging/link-first.spec.ts` then drops the second sign-in.

## 5. Risk and shared files

- **Fix 1** changes the render name of the shared folder's root. The focus leg reads that name through `scope_root_record_name` (`facade.rs:4139`) to walk back a lagging record. R1 is the correct name for that walk.
- **Fix 2** sends one more event each time the set changes. This costs little, because the store merges pulls that overlap.
- **Shared hot files:**
  - `crates/engine/src/facade.rs` is touched by all three defects. #2022 is in `scope_sharing`, with owner state left stale after another device's write-scope cut. That is the same class of defect: a stale device-local root name.
  - `grants/received_status.rs` is touched by #2023, and possibly by #2024 (the state of a cut person's bookmark drives the invite page to `joined`).
  - The invite route in `apps/web` and `grants/invite*.rs` belong to #2024.
- **Batching:** put #2022 and #2023 in one PR.</result>

# Diagnosis #2022: owner device A reads no sharing state after device B's write-scope cut (engine)

## Root cause
- B's cut raises only B's floor. The write-scope cut on B runs a write wave, moves the folder root and seals its owner-write-blob at write epoch 2. B raises only its own write-epoch floor (crates/engine/src/facade/claim_conversion.rs:835).
- A keeps floor 1 (durable; a new sign-in keeps it) from its own link mint.
- The owner recovers the write scope seed only at the standing floor (crates/engine/src/net/adopter.rs:640-653, open_write_scope_seed_at). The epoch-2 blob does not open at floor 1, so write_scope_seed is None; write_plane_of_gated gives ResolveFailure::Unavailable (crates/engine/src/net/rotation.rs:1602).
- scope_sharing (crates/engine/src/facade.rs:11774, `resolve_anchored(...).ok()?`) turns that into state: None. Every owner action on the folder uses the same resolve (OwnerRotationNet::gated_write_plane, rotation.rs:1805-1822); a link mint on A fails with Seam("descendant record unavailable").
- Nothing raises A's floor to 2. Only a scope-pointer consult (net/pointer_fetch.rs:134) raises the floor of a device that did not run the wave, and none of the three consult paths runs on A:
  - Tick walk: ScopeWalk::recover_write_plane_from_pointer (rotation.rs:1401-1406) returns early while a floor stands (a fresh device has no floor, so it consults and seeds floor 2: that is why a third device works).
  - Polled tick consult: consults only FocusWindow::open_shared_scopes (sync/tick.rs:166); no production code fills that field.
  - On-access consult: owner access paths build nets with PointerConsultArm::Refused; ConsultReason::OnAccess (sync/pointer.rs:54) has no caller.
- Content reads still work because the cut does not change the read plane.

## Why tests missed it
- a_write_claim_converts_on_the_other_owner_devices_tick_with_one_cut (crates/engine/tests/owner_actions.rs:5480) asserts the sharing read only on the converting device. a_claim_converts_on_the_owners_other_device uses a read link (no write wave). The #1646 tests cover a device with no floor, not a device whose floor is below the pointer's write epoch.

## Fix
In OwnerRotationNet::gated_write_plane (rotation.rs), the one function all owner resolves use:
1. When write_plane_of_gated gives Unavailable at RootAnchor::Descendant and the section holds an owner-write-blob, run an on-access PointerConsult::run for the scope (raises the write floor on sight).
2. Reopen the blob at the new floor, set root.write_scope_seed, read the write plane again.
3. Pointer absent/unavailable -> Unavailable. Consult rejects the pointer -> Rejected.
4. rotation.rs:2997 is a second write_plane_of_gated site (sweep path); check whether it needs the same.
Invariants: a rejected pointer maps to ResolveFailure::Rejected -> EngineError::TrustViolation via from_resolve_failure, never Unavailable; scope_sharing must emit a trust-violation event for a rejection instead of swallowing it. Floors stay monotonic (only PointerConsult raises, only to the epoch the owner signed). Stale-copy case (pointer epoch == floor, blob still does not open) stays Unavailable. No encode change, no clock/RNG/debug_assert. Update the PointerConsultArm doc (a Refused pass consults nothing) to name the on-access consult, or pass a ConsultReason::OnAccess arm.
Blueprint: blueprint/engine.md "Pointer planes": "the pointer resolve joins the focus-window tick for open shared scopes, runs on access for cached ones, and is the first act on cold start." CONTEXT.md "Scope pointer" and "Floor law" (floors "cold-seed from the re-point object's owner-vouched epochs").
Optional: ScopeWalk::recover_write_plane_from_pointer can also consult when a floor stands and the blob does not open, paced by pointer_consult_interval.

# Diagnosis #2023: a write link holder keeps a read view after conversion (engine)

## Root cause
- The write link join adds the shared folder to the render tree at the old scope root name R0. merge_grafted (crates/engine/src/grants/received_status.rs:233, the None arm near 253) sets meta.ipns_name only when it creates the node.
- The conversion does a write-scope cut, which moves the scope root to R1 (crates/engine/src/facade/claim_conversion.rs:618-647, cut_write_scope at 810).
- The bookmark moves to R1 by the pointer heal (follow_held_pointers / HoldChange::Heal) and by the accept_share reconcile (grants/accept.rs:1231). The personal blob opens at R1; the write seed is deposited against R1. /shared shows granted, write, via-link=false.
- The render node keeps R0: the Some(meta) arm (received_status.rs:248-251) only renames, never updates ipns_name.
- The drain uses R0: grafted_write_passes (facade.rs:5035-5068) takes its name from base.node(root).ipns_name; the drain scope uses root_name: &pass.name (facade.rs:7751-7760). The R1 write seed does not derive R0; the drain treats it as name skew and waits with no event (sync/drain.rs:7515). No write from that session lands. A new session adds the folder from the bookmark at R1, so it works.
- Evidence: a test in owner_actions.rs (patch diag-repro-and-fix.patch): same session before the fix, a queued create stays queued each pass with no dead letter; new session drains at once; same session with the fix drains. 1968 lib tests + 190 owner_actions tests pass with the fix.
- Open point: the e2e reports snapshot permission 'read'; in the engine test permission changed to Write one tick after the row did. Likely cause: grafted_write_roots is set at facade.rs:7602 before the received-share pass at facade.rs:7972 deposits the seed, so the permission changes one tick later and no SnapshotUpdated event comes with it; a host view painted between those ticks stays read until another event or a pull (the web pulls only on a successful manualRefresh, apps/web/src/engine/snapshotStore.ts). This lag also fits the write-grant.spec.ts flake with 2 workers.

## Why tests missed it
received_status.rs a_root_a_write_wave_moved_still_opens_through_the_pointer checks the healed bookmark and listing, not the render node's ipns_name. owner_actions.rs write-link tests check only the owner side. The WriteGrantee harness (facade.rs tests near 19700) accepts a write grant directly so its node already has the final name. The name-skew wait sends no event.

## Fix
1. merge_grafted (grants/received_status.rs): when the node exists and its ipns_name differs from share.scope_root_name, set it to the bookmark name; include that change in the SnapshotUpdated condition (~10 lines, tested in the patch).
2. facade.rs near 7602: when the new grafted_write_roots set differs from the old one, send Event::SnapshotUpdated so the host repaints on the tick that proves or drops a write pass.
Invariants: the name comes only from the verified bookmark, healed by the owner-signed pointer (ADR 0024 D5 step 3) or the gated accept_share, never from a record's own word; seed_names / deposit_write_seed (facade.rs:4801-4825) stays the proof that the seed names the root; gate rejection stays TrustViolation; no debug_assert, clock, RNG, wire change.
Normative: ADR 0024 D4 ("At conversion the owner engine mints the personal row at the conversion permission, with the write material and a write-scope cut when the folder has none yet ... The grantee then writes under its own writer pseudonym."), ADR 0024 D2, ADR 0023 (each URL holder becomes a writer after conversion, with no owner step).

## Regression tests
- owner_actions.rs (GrantScenario, mint_link_at(Permission::Write), a holder session on fx.recipient_device, a phone at the owner identity converting on its tick): holder claims and ticks until the link read shows the folder; phone ticks and converts; holder ticks twice; assert snapshot(shared).permission == Write; send Command::Create under the shared root and tick; assert the queue is empty and the owner lists the child at the moved root.
- Unit assertion in a_root_a_write_wave_moved_still_opens_through_the_pointer: the render node of SCOPE has ipns_name == scope_root_name().
- For fix 2: assert SnapshotUpdated is sent on the tick where the root enters grafted_write_roots.

## Risk
Fix 1 changes the render name of the shared root; the focus leg reads that name through scope_root_record_name (facade.rs:4139) to walk back a lagging record, and R1 is the correct name for that walk. Fix 2 sends one more event per set change. Hot files: facade.rs (all three defects), grants/received_status.rs (#2023, maybe #2024).

The two expected failures mark two product defects that the new suite found. Each is a real bug on `main`, not a test problem. The tests stay in the suite so the defect is visible, and the marks make the suite green until the fix lands.

- **Step 5, device A revokes the write link (#2022).** When device B converts a write-link claim, it moves the folder's root and raises only its own write-epoch floor. Device A keeps its old floor, cannot open the new root blob, and its share dialog shows "people unavailable". So device A cannot revoke the link. The mark is keyed on that symptom: it becomes an expected failure only when device A shows "people unavailable" after the setup. Any other failure reports red.
- **Step 4, the joined session writes (#2023).** A session that joined through a write link keeps the old root name in its render tree after the conversion. Its writes wait forever on a name skew, so the session stays read-only until a new sign-in. The mark states that symptom. The other step 4 test signs the writer in again, which is the workaround, and passes.

A third defect (#2024, a cut person cannot join again through a new link) has no mark, because the test works around it with a direct grant by contact code.

The marks also protect against a silent fix. Playwright reports an unexpected pass as a failure, so the fix PR must remove the marks in the same change.

That fix PR is in progress on branch `fix/2022-2023-2024-link-first-stale-roots`. Two of the three engine fixes are committed with regression tests. The third is under way. After PR 2025 merges, the same PR removes both marks, drops the second sign-in, and changes step 6 to a join through a new link.

Umbrella #1963 is complete and closed. All 22 sub-issues are closed, every PR in this thread is linked and merged, and the close-out comment on #1963 lists the batch-to-PR map.

**Merged in this last stretch**

| PR | What | Merge |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1994 | invite page preview | 53191d913 |
| 1993 | share dialog, link as the main path | 9ceec6e12 |
| 1998 | sharing docs rewrite | 55d125ea0 |
| 2025 | two-device link-first e2e | 46a4d2abc |
| 2027 | docs follow-up for the two Greptile findings on PR 2005 | 9feb639d5 |
| 2026 | engine fixes for #2022, #2023, #2024 | 28e806252 |

**What the e2e found and PR 2026 fixed**

- An owner device that did not run the write wave kept its old write-epoch floor and read no sharing state. An owner access now consults the scope pointer when the owner-write-blob does not open.
- A session that joined through a write link kept the old root name in its render tree, so its writes never landed. The healed bookmark now moves the render name, and the tick reports the change.
- The engine treated a cut bookmark as a join, so the invite page hid the join. The link read now checks the owner-signed set. ADR 0028 D5 is narrowed in cipher-box-next#109, which is merged.

**Review gates.** PR 2026 had the Fable review with the crypto-privacy pass, which found one blocker in the mint probe, folded before the CodeRabbit pass. CodeRabbit gave two minor findings, both fixed with tests. Greptile had no credits from about 12:00 UTC, per your ruling.

**Housekeeping.** All lane worktrees are removed and the disk has 79 GiB free. Memory holds the Greptile credit note and the Opus session-limit note, and the learnings file has the session entries.

**Open outside the umbrella**

- #1984 stays open by design.
- The staging link-first spec runs inside the next tag-staging run. It was typechecked only, so that run is its first measurement.
